title.zh: 卷421 列傳二百八 沈兆霖 曹毓瑛 许乃普子：彭寿 赵光 朱嶟 李菡 张祥河 罗惇衍 郑敦谨 庞鍾璐
title.en: Volume 421 Biographies 208: Shen Zhaolin, Cao Yuying, Xu Naipu Son: Peng Shou, Zhao Guang, Zhu Zun, Li Han, Zhang Xianghe, Luo Dunyan, Zheng Dunjin, Pang Zhonglu
title.raw: 卷421 列傳二百八 沈兆霖 曹毓瑛 许乃普子：彭寿 赵光 朱嶟 李菡 张祥河 罗惇衍 郑敦谨 庞鍾璐

sentences.zh: =沈兆霖=沈兆霖，字朗亭，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Shen Zhaolin, styled Langting, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhaolin, courtesy name Langting, was from Qiantang, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of the Daoguang reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a Compiler.

sentences.zh: 十九年，大考二等。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, in the triennial evaluation he received the second grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he earned the second grade in the triennial evaluation.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遷司業。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was transferred to be Vice-Director of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to the post of Vice-Director of Studies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷侍講，入直上書房，授惇郡王讀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was transferred to be Reader-in-Waiting, entered the Upper Study, and was appointed to instruct the Prince of Dun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he became a Reader-in-Waiting, entered service in the Upper Study, and was appointed tutor to the Prince of Dun.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷侍講學士，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was transferred to be Doctor Reader-in-Waiting and served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Doctor Reader-in-Waiting and assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 歷詹事、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Junior Tutor and Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Junior Tutor and as Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，擢吏部侍郎，督江西學政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and appointed Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and made Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪自武昌下九江，兆霖請速援南昌。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Guangdong rebels advanced from Wuchang down to Jiujiang; Zhaolin requested urgent relief for Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, as the Taiping rebels pushed from Wuchang toward Jiujiang, Zhaolin urged that Nanchang be reinforced at once.

sentences.zh: 上諮以軍事，兆霖奏言：「江西會城雖暫可無慮，賊擾外府，省兵不能兼顧。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted him on military affairs; Zhaolin memorialized: "Although the provincial capital of Jiangxi may for the moment be secure, the rebels are harassing the outer prefectures and the provincial troops cannot cover everything.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked his view on military affairs, Zhaolin memorialized: "Although the provincial capital of Jiangxi may be safe for the moment, the rebels are raiding the outlying prefectures, and the provincial troops cannot be everywhere at once.

sentences.zh: 外府各有團練，如肯齊心協力，何藉分兵？

translations.literal: Each outer prefecture has its own militia; if they would unite in common effort, why need troops be divided?
translations.idiomatic: Each outlying prefecture already has local militia; if they would act together, why must regular troops be split up to defend them?

sentences.zh: 即如撫州鄉團不下數万，皆留保本村，官兵祗三百，已調赴會城。

translations.literal: Take Fuzhou as an example: the village militia number no fewer than tens of thousands, yet all remain to defend their own villages; the government troops number only three hundred and have already been moved to the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuzhou, for instance, village militia number in the tens of thousands, yet all stay home to guard their own hamlets, while the government garrison is only three hundred men—and those have already been called to the capital.

sentences.zh: 如團練不能合力，賊至何以御之？

translations.literal: If the militia cannot combine their strength, when the rebels arrive how can they be resisted?
translations.idiomatic: If the militia cannot fight as one, how will they resist the rebels when they come?

sentences.zh: 其故皆因堅壁清野，舊議祗守本村，並不出戰，不知事與嘉慶間川、楚教匪不同。

translations.literal: The reason is that under the policy of fortifying walls and clearing the countryside, the old practice was only to defend one's own village and never to go out to fight, without realizing that the situation differs from the Sichuan and Hubei sect rebels of the Jiaqing period.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble is the "fortify and clear" doctrine: the old rule was to hold one's own village and never march out, as if this war were the same as the sectarian rebellions in Sichuan and Hubei under Jiaqing—but it is not.

sentences.zh: 川、楚教匪劫掠村莊，自以堅守堡寨為是，今賊專攻省會、郡縣城池，城既破，鄉勇亦相與解散矣。

translations.literal: The Sichuan and Hubei sect rebels plundered villages, so holding fast to fortified stockades was correct; now the rebels concentrate on attacking provincial capitals and prefectural and county cities—once a city falls, the village braves disperse together.
translations.idiomatic: Those sect rebels looted the countryside, so clinging to fortified hamlets made sense; today's enemy strikes provincial and prefectural seats. Once a city falls, the village militia scatter with it.

sentences.zh: 撫州如此，各省各府亦必皆然。

translations.literal: If Fuzhou is thus, every province and prefecture must be the same.
translations.idiomatic: What is true of Fuzhou will be true everywhere else.

sentences.zh: 乞飭直省當於練勇中精選十之二三，聯爲鄉兵，統以練達有位望之人。

translations.literal: I beg that each province be ordered to select two or three tenths of the best from among the trained braves, unite them as local troops, and place them under experienced men of standing.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each province pick the best two or three men in ten from its trained militia, form them into local companies, and put them under capable leaders of local standing.

sentences.zh: 遇本縣有警，互相救援。

translations.literal: When any county in the group is alarmed, they shall rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: When any county in the network is attacked, the others should come to its aid.

sentences.zh: 其外府、外縣仍不得調往，以免擾累。」

translations.literal: Troops from other prefectures and counties must still not be transferred away, so as to avoid disturbance and burden."
translations.idiomatic: Men from other prefectures and counties should still not be drafted away, so the people are not harassed further."

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: The memorial received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋以病乞罷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 五年，病痊，署吏部侍郎，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when his illness was cured, he served as acting Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and continued in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, recovered from illness, he returned as acting Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and resumed duty in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 兆霖疏言：「安徽各郡，江北安、廬、和，江南池、太，皆為賊踞。

translations.literal: Zhaolin memorialized: "In Anhui's various prefectures, on the north of the river An, Lu, and He, and on the south of the river Chi and Tai, all are occupied by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin wrote: "Across Anhui, the northern prefectures of Anqing, Luzhou, and Hezhou and the southern prefectures of Chizhou and Taiping are all in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 巡撫駐廬州，東北徽、寧、廣三屬，幾為巡撫號令所不及。

translations.literal: The governor-general is stationed at Luzhou; the three circuits of Huizhou, Ningguo, and Guangde in the northeast lie almost beyond the reach of his orders.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general sits at Luzhou, while Huizhou, Ningguo, and Guangde in the northeast lie almost outside his command.

sentences.zh: 事急則向浙江請餉，事平則洩沓如前，不加整飭，旋收旋失，糜餉殃民。

translations.literal: When matters are urgent they ask Zhejiang for funds; when calm returns they are slack as before, without rectification—gains are quickly lost, funds are wasted, and the people suffer.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis they beg Zhejiang for pay; in quiet they lapse into the old slackness, never tightening control—ground won is ground lost, money is squandered, and the people pay the price.

sentences.zh: 臣察徽、寧二府，山川險固，地皆可守，民亦健奮，歙、休寧二縣，尤多富民。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that in the two prefectures of Huizhou and Ningguo the mountains and rivers are rugged and defensible, the land can all be held, and the people are sturdy and spirited; in the two counties of She and Xiuning there are especially many wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: I find that Huizhou and Ningguo are rugged and defensible, their people hardy and willing to fight; She and Xiuning counties in particular abound in wealthy families.

sentences.zh: 宜於皖南設大員，專轄四府、一州，庶以飭吏治，固民心。

translations.literal: A high official should be placed in southern Anhui with sole jurisdiction over four prefectures and one department, so that official discipline may be enforced and popular loyalty secured.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Anhui needs a senior commissioner with sole charge of four prefectures and one department, to tighten administration and win the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 度險設防，皖撫得專心於江北，浙撫亦不至牽制於皖南。」

translations.literal: Assessing the terrain and setting defenses, the Anhui governor can concentrate on the north of the river, and the Zhejiang governor will not be hampered by southern Anhui."
translations.idiomatic: With defenses planned for the terrain, the Anhui governor can focus on the north bank, and the Zhejiang governor will not be pulled into southern Anhui."

sentences.zh: 疏下廷議，改池太道為皖南道，得專摺奏事，如福建台灣道例，從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for court deliberation; the Chitai Circuit was changed to the Southern Anhui Circuit, empowered to submit memorials on its own authority, following the precedent of the Taiwan Circuit in Fujian—and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated the proposal and approved it: the Chitai Circuit became the Southern Anhui Circuit, with authority to memorialize the throne directly, as with the Taiwan circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 尋兼署工、兵二部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also served concurrently as acting head of the Boards of Works and War.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added concurrent acting appointments at the Boards of Works and War.

sentences.zh: 六年，授吏部侍郎，調工部，復調戶部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office, transferred to the Board of Works, and then transferred again to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office, then moved to Works and then to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，命往通州察覈通濟庫，奏請如戶部三庫例，以倉場侍郎兼管，佩印鑰，著為令。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was ordered to Tongzhou to inspect the Tongji Granary; he memorialized that, following the precedent of the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue, the Granary Commissioner should concurrently manage it, bearing seal and keys—and this was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent to Tongzhou to audit the Tongji Granary and proposed that, as with the Board of Revenue's three treasuries, the Granary Commissioner should manage it concurrently, bearing seal and keys—a rule then made permanent.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十年，署戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he served as acting Minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting Minister of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七月，英吉利、法蘭西兵內犯，兆霖疏請專講守禦，勿汲汲言撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, English and French troops invaded inland; Zhaolin memorialized urging that defense alone be stressed and that one not be eager to speak of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, as British and French forces advanced inland, Zhaolin urged the court to focus on defense and not rush toward negotiation.

sentences.zh: 九月，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he was appointed Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Minister of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 撫議既定，上猶駐熱河，兆霖與諸大臣奏請回鑾，上命待明年。

translations.literal: After the peace negotiations were settled, the emperor still remained at Rehe; Zhaolin and the other grand ministers memorialized requesting the return of the imperial procession, but the emperor ordered that they wait until the next year.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was made, yet the emperor still stayed at Rehe; Zhaolin and his colleagues asked him to return to Beijing, but he told them to wait until the following year.

sentences.zh: 兆霖復奏請明年春融，即啟蹕還京。

translations.literal: Zhaolin again memorialized asking that as soon as the ice melted the following spring, the imperial procession should set out to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin pressed again that the court should leave as soon as the roads thawed in spring.

sentences.zh: 尋調戶部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred back to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗回鑾即位，命充軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Muzong Emperor returned and took the throne, Zhaolin was appointed a Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the Tongzhi Emperor returned to Beijing and ascended the throne, Zhaolin was made a Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 甘肅西寧撒回為亂，總督樂斌遣提督成瑞​​率兵討之，逗撓不進。

translations.literal: The Salar Muslims of Xining in Gansu rose in rebellion; Governor-General Yue Bin sent Regional Commander Cheng Rui to lead troops against them, but he dallied and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Salar Muslims of Xining, Gansu, rebelled; Governor-General Yue Bin sent Regional Commander Cheng Rui against them, but Cheng stalled and would not march.

sentences.zh: 樂斌用西寧辦事大臣多慧議招撫，亂久未定。

translations.literal: Yue Bin followed the pacification proposals of Duo Hui, Commissioner for Xining Affairs, and the rebellion long remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Bin adopted the conciliation plan of Duo Hui, the Xining commissioner, and the revolt dragged on.

sentences.zh: 上命兆霖偕尚書麟魁往按，盡發樂斌等瞻徇貽誤狀，樂斌戍新疆，成瑞、多慧逮京治罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhaolin together with Minister Lin Kui to go investigate; they fully exposed how Yue Bin and others had shown favoritism and caused delay; Yue Bin was banished to Xinjiang, and Cheng Rui and Duo Hui were brought to the capital for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhaolin with Minister Lin Kui to investigate; they exposed Yue Bin's favoritism and delay—Yue was exiled to Xinjiang, and Cheng Rui and Duo Hui were brought to Beijing for trial.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，命兆霖署陝甘總督，親督兵自碾伯進擊撒回，屢敗之，撒回乞降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Zhaolin was appointed acting Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu; he personally led troops from Nianbo to attack the Salar rebels, repeatedly defeated them, and the Salars begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was made acting Governor-General of Shaanxi-Gansu, led the army from Nianbo against the Salars, routed them repeatedly, and they sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 七月，師還，次平番二道嶺溝，雨雹，山水驟發，兆霖及從行兵役並沒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, as the army returned and halted at Erdao Linggou in Pingfan, rain and hail fell and mountain floods suddenly burst forth; Zhaolin and all the soldiers and attendants with him were drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on the march home, the column halted at Erdao Linggou in Pingfan; hail fell and a flash flood swept down—Zhaolin and every man with him were drowned.

sentences.zh: 水退，得兆霖屍，猶端坐輿中。

translations.literal: When the water receded, Zhaolin's body was found, still sitting upright in his sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: When the waters fell, his body was found still seated upright in his sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 布政使恩麟以聞，上深惜之，賜卹，贈太子太保，諡文忠。

translations.literal: Financial Commissioner En Lin reported this; the emperor deeply mourned him, granted condolence gifts, posthumously promoted him to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Financial Commissioner En Lin reported the death; the emperor mourned him deeply, granted funeral honors, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Wenzhong, "Loyal and Upright."

sentences.zh: =曹毓瑛=曹毓瑛，字琢如，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Cao Yuying, styled Zhuoru, was a native of Jiangyin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuying, courtesy name Zhuoru, was from Jiangyin, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十七年拔貢，授兵部七品小京官，遷主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Daoguang he was a selected tribute student from the provincial examination, appointed a seventh-rank clerk in the Board of War, promoted to Director, and served as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a tribute scholar in the seventeenth year of Daoguang, he entered the Board of War as a seventh-rank clerk, rose to Director, and served on the Grand Council staff.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，舉順天鄉試，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was promoted again to Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he passed the metropolitan provincial examination and was promoted again to Bureau Director.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，擢鴻臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 時江南大營潰，總督何桂清棄常州，蘇、常相繼陷。

translations.literal: At that time the great Jiangnan camp collapsed; Governor-General He Guiqing abandoned Changzhou, and Suzhou and Changzhou fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The great Jiangnan army camp had just collapsed; Governor-General He Guiqing fled Changzhou, and Suzhou and Changzhou fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 毓瑛疏陳軍事，略曰：「拯溺救焚，其事宜急而不宜緩。

translations.literal: Yuying memorialized on military affairs, stating in summary: "To save the drowning and extinguish the burning, the matter should be urgent and not slow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuying laid out a military plan, writing in part: "Rescue must come quickly, not slowly.

sentences.zh: 搗虛批亢，其事宜合而不宜分。

translations.literal: To strike the empty and attack the vital, the matter should be united and not divided.
translations.idiomatic: Strikes at the enemy's weak points must be coordinated, not scattered.

sentences.zh: 臣前讀都興阿奏，擬自英山由豫境繞赴徐、宿，以達江北，而曾國籓通籌方略，擬分三路進剿，俟八月大舉。

translations.literal: Your servant has read Du Xing'a's memorial proposing to go from Yingshan through Henan territory by a detour to Xuzhou and Suzhou to reach the north bank of the Yangtze, while Zeng Guofan in his overall plan proposes a three-route advance, waiting until the eighth month for a major campaign.
translations.idiomatic: I have read Du Xing'a's plan to march from Yingshan through Henan to Xuzhou and Suzhou and reach the north bank, and Zeng Guofan's scheme for a three-pronged advance in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 竊謂都興阿由豫境以達江北，程途紆遠，非兩月不能到。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to say that for Du Xing'a to reach the north bank through Henan, the route is circuitous and he cannot arrive in less than two months.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a's detour through Henan is so long that he cannot reach the north bank in under two months.

sentences.zh: 浙江自蕭翰慶陣亡，江長貴自平望退守，銳氣盡消。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang, since Xiao Hanqing fell in battle and Jiang Changgui retreated from Pingwang to hold defense, fighting spirit has been entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhejiang, after Xiao Hanqing was killed and Jiang Changgui fell back from Pingwang, morale has collapsed.

sentences.zh: 以屢潰之孱兵，禦剽悍之勍賊，待至八月，松、太、杭、嘉、湖諸郡勢將瓦解，蔓延愈廣，規复愈難。

translations.literal: With repeatedly routed weak troops to oppose fierce and powerful rebels, if we wait until the eighth month, the prefectures of Songjiang, Taicang, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou will be on the verge of collapse; the rebellion will spread wider and recovery will grow harder.
translations.idiomatic: Weak troops that have been routed again and again cannot hold off fierce rebels—wait until August and Songjiang, Taicang, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou will crumble; the rebellion will spread and recovery will be harder still.

sentences.zh: 為今計者，都興阿宜自英、霍取道臨、鳳以抵江北，不過旬日，即由通、泰渡江，直抵江陰，進攻常州、無錫為一路，而以周沐潤所募沙勇副之；

translations.literal: For the present plan, Du Xing'a should go from Ying and Huo by way of Lin and Feng to reach the north bank—in no more than ten days he can cross the river from Tong and Tai, strike straight for Jiangyin, and advance on Changzhou and Wuxi as one route, with the sand-boat braves raised by Zhou Murun as support;
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a should march from Yingzhou and Huozhou through Linhuai and Fengyang to the north bank—within ten days he can cross from Tongzhou and Taizhou, land at Jiangyin, and drive on Changzhou and Wuxi as one column, supported by Zhou Murun's river braves;

sentences.zh: 鎮江現有兵萬餘，巴棟阿、馮子材、向奎進規丹陽為一路；

translations.literal: At Zhenjiang there are now more than ten thousand troops; Ba Dong'e, Feng Zicai, and Xiang Kui should advance on Danyang as one route;
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang already has ten thousand men—Ba Dong'e, Feng Zicai, and Xiang Kui should press Danyang as a second column;

sentences.zh: 薛煥在上海增募勇丁萬人，由嘉定、太倉、崑山進攻蘇州為一路，而命張玉良出嘉興、平望以副之；

translations.literal: Xue Huan at Shanghai should raise ten thousand more braves and advance on Suzhou from Jiading, Taicang, and Kunshan as one route, while Zhang Yuliang is ordered out from Jiaxing and Pingwang in support;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huan should recruit ten thousand more men at Shanghai and attack Suzhou from Jiading, Taicang, and Kunshan as a third column, with Zhang Yuliang moving from Jiaxing and Pingwang in support;

sentences.zh: 曾國籓率楚師由寧國取道廣德，進抵嘉、湖為一路，策應諸軍，而令米興朝攻宜興、溧陽，週天受攻高淳、東壩，曾秉忠督長龍船入太湖以副之。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan should lead the Hunan army from Ningguo by way of Guangde to reach Jiaxing and Huzhou as one route, coordinating the other armies, while Mi Xingchao attacks Yixing and Liyang, Zhou Tianshou attacks Gaochun and Dongba, and Zeng Bingzhong leads the long dragon boats into Lake Tai in support.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan should lead his Hunan troops from Ningguo through Guangde into Jiaxing and Huzhou as a fourth column to coordinate the rest, while Mi Xingchao strikes Yixing and Liyang, Zhou Tianshou takes Gaochun and Dongba, and Zeng Bingzhong sends the long dragon boats into Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 攻賊之所必救，據賊之所必爭。

translations.literal: Attack where the rebels must come to the rescue; hold what the rebels must contest.
translations.idiomatic: Strike where the enemy must respond; seize what he cannot afford to lose.

sentences.zh: 俟曾國籓新募勇至，然後分路進剿，庶於事有濟。」

translations.literal: Wait until Zeng Guofan's newly recruited braves arrive, and then advance by separate routes to suppress the rebels—only thus may the affair succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Only after Zeng Guofan's new recruits arrive should the columns move out separately—then there may be hope of success."

sentences.zh: 英、法兩國合兵犯京師，上幸熱河，軍書旁午，樞臣未全從，上命擇章京資深才優者佐諸大臣辦事。

translations.literal: Britain and France combined their armies and attacked the capital; the emperor went to Rehe; military dispatches poured in thick and fast; the Grand Councilors did not all follow, and the emperor ordered that a clerk of long service and superior talent be chosen to assist the grand ministers in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Britain and France marched on Beijing and the emperor fled to Rehe, dispatches flooded in; not all Grand Councilors had followed him, and he ordered that a senior, capable clerk be chosen to assist the ministers still at court.

sentences.zh: 毓瑛在直久，諸大臣欲舉以應，固辭，遂越次用焦祐瀛。

translations.literal: Yuying had long served in the Grand Council; the grand ministers wished to nominate him to answer the order, but he firmly declined, and Jiao Youying was appointed out of turn instead.
translations.idiomatic: Yuying had served on the council staff for years; the ministers wanted to name him, but he firmly declined, and Jiao Youying was appointed ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，諸大臣皆譴罷，乃命毓瑛在軍機大臣上學習行走，遷順天府丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne, the grand ministers were all censured and dismissed; then Yuying was ordered to study under the Grand Councilors, and was transferred to be Vice Governor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when Tongzhi took the throne, the old councilors were dismissed; Yuying was attached to the Grand Council as a trainee and made Vice Governor of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，遷大理寺卿，授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he was transferred to be President of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed a Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he became President of the Court of Judicial Review and a full Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢工部侍郎，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of Works and transferred to the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and transferred to War.

sentences.zh: 三年，江南平，加頭品頂戴，賜花翎，署兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Jiangnan was pacified, he was granted the first-rank button, awarded the peacock feather, and served as acting Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after Jiangnan was pacified, he received the first-rank court button and peacock feather and served as acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢左都御史，尋授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, and soon afterward was appointed Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Left Censor-in-Chief and soon after Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，贈太子少保，諡恭愨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Gongque.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Gongque, "Respectful and Cautious."

sentences.zh: 方端華、肅順擅政，毓瑛獨不附。

translations.literal: When Duanhua and Sushun monopolized power, Yuying alone would not attach himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Duanhua and Sushun dominated the court, Yuying alone refused to join their faction.

sentences.zh: 及佐樞政，廉慎勿懈，每謂：「軍旅大事，患在信任不專，事權不一。

translations.literal: When he assisted in council affairs, he was incorruptible and cautious without slackening, and often said: "In great military matters, the trouble lies in trust not being concentrated and authority not being unified.
translations.idiomatic: In council he remained scrupulous and tireless, and often said: "The curse of military affairs is divided trust and split command.

sentences.zh: 古來良將，率以掣肘不能成功。」

translations.literal: Good generals of old mostly failed to succeed because they were checked and restrained."
translations.idiomatic: History's best generals have usually been ruined by interference from above."

sentences.zh: 時以為名言雲。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: Men at the time took this for a maxim.

sentences.zh: =許乃普=許乃普，字滇生，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Xu Naipu, styled Diansheng, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Naipu, courtesy name Diansheng, was from Qiantang, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 拔貢，考授七品小京官，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: As a selected tribute student, he passed the examination and was appointed a seventh-rank clerk in the capital, and served as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a tribute scholar, he passed the capital examination for a seventh-rank clerk and joined the Grand Council staff.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年，成一甲二名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing, he placed second in the first class of the jinshi examination and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing he took second place in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was appointed a Compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang, he served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daoguang he entered the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 四年，大考二等，擢洗馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, in the triennial evaluation he received the second grade and was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he earned the second grade in the triennial evaluation and was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，督貴州學政，任滿回京，仍直南書房，累遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Guizhou; when his term ended he returned to the capital, again served in the Southern Study, and was promoted in succession to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became Educational Commissioner of Guizhou; when his term ended he returned to the Southern Study and rose to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復以大考二等擢侍講學士，督江西學政，三遷內閣​​學士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, again with the second grade in the triennial evaluation he was promoted to Doctor Reader-in-Waiting, appointed Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi, and promoted three times to Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he again took second grade in the evaluation, became Doctor Reader-in-Waiting, served as Educational Commissioner of Jiangxi, and rose three ranks to Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢刑部侍郎，罷直南書房，專治部事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of Punishments, left the Southern Study, and devoted himself solely to the affairs of his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he became Vice Minister of Punishments, left the Southern Study, and focused on his ministry.

sentences.zh: 調吏部，又調戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Board of Civil Office, and then to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Civil Office, then to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he was promoted to Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，坐事鐫五級，補太常寺少卿，遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, on account of an offense he was demoted five ranks, appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and transferred to be Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was demoted five ranks for an offense, appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and then Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗御極，命仍直南書房。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Wenzong Emperor took the throne, he was ordered to resume service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, he was ordered back to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 詔求言，乃普疏言：「方今先務，莫急於正君心，培聖德。

translations.literal: An edict sought opinions; Naipu memorialized: "At present the foremost task is none more urgent than rectifying the ruler's mind and cultivating sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne called for candid advice, Naipu wrote: "Nothing matters more now than rectifying the emperor's mind and nurturing his virtue.

sentences.zh: 請敕館臣合列朝聖訓，依類分門，排日進呈，庶政奉以為宗。

translations.literal: I ask that the Hanlin scholars be ordered to compile the sacred instructions of successive reigns, arrange them by category and section, and present them day by day, so that governance may take them as its standard.
translations.idiomatic: Have the Hanlin compile the sacred instructions of past reigns by topic and present them day by day, so that government may take them as its guide.

sentences.zh: 恩詔各省保舉孝廉方正，請敕下各直省學政考覈學官，學官得人，所舉庶幾可恃。

translations.literal: An amnesty edict directed each province to recommend filial and upright scholars; I ask that each provincial educational commissioner be ordered to examine the local school officials—for if the school officials are worthy, the recommendations may be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty edict calls for recommending filial and upright men from each province; order the educational commissioners to inspect local school officials—worthy teachers will yield trustworthy nominees.

sentences.zh: 刑部於致死胞伯叔及胞兄之案，以事關服制，往往夾簽聲明，並非有心干犯，巧為開脫。

translations.literal: The Board of Punishments, in cases of killing one's father's younger brothers or one's elder brother of the same mother, because the matter concerns mourning obligations often inserts a slip stating that there was no intent to violate and artfully seeks exoneration.
translations.idiomatic: In cases of killing a paternal uncle or an elder brother, the Board of Punishments often slips in a note that mourning obligations were involved and there was no deliberate violation—an artful way to let offenders off.

sentences.zh: 請​​敕下刑部斟情酌理，俾無枉縱。

translations.literal: I ask that the Board of Punishments be ordered to weigh circumstances and reason, so that none are wrongly spared or wrongly punished.
translations.idiomatic: Order the Board of Punishments to weigh each case on its merits, so that none escape unjustly and none are punished unjustly.

sentences.zh: 各省綠營弁兵平時宜加意訓練，武職到京，兵部驗看時，當令兼演火器。」

translations.literal: The Green Standard officers and soldiers of each province should in ordinary times be trained with special care; when military officials come to the capital and the Board of War inspects them, they should also be made to drill with firearms."
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard troops in every province should train harder in peacetime; when officers come to Beijing for inspection, the Board of War should require them to demonstrate firearms as well."

sentences.zh: 疏上，得旨：「下所司議奏。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the imperial rescript read: "Send down to the responsible offices for deliberation and memorial."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Refer this to the relevant offices for deliberation."

sentences.zh: 復申諭刑部及各督撫，服制案罪名務得實情。

translations.literal: He further reiterated to the Board of Punishments and all governors-general and governors that in mourning-obligation cases the charges must accord with the true facts.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed the Board of Punishments and all governors that charges in mourning-obligation cases must reflect the true facts.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 乃普疏論軍營奏報欺飾，得旨，令各路統兵大臣及各督撫力除積習，嚴為稽察，其朦混掩飾者，據實嚴參。

translations.literal: Naipu memorialized on the deception and concealment in military camp reports; he received an imperial rescript ordering commanders-in-chief on every route and all governors-general and governors to strive to remove entrenched abuses, conduct strict inspection, and impeach according to fact those who confused and covered up the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Naipu wrote on falsified military reports; the emperor ordered every field commander and governor to root out the old habit of deception, inspect strictly, and impeach anyone who concealed the truth.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪陷九江，擾皖北，覬覦北鄉，而廬、鳳守禦單弱，乃普疏請調黑龍江兵，道山東、江南，徑赴安徽，遠可張蘇、浙之聲援，近可固廬、鳳之門戶。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Cantonese rebels captured Jiujiang, harassed northern Anhui, and cast covetous eyes on Beixiang; but the defenses of Luzhou and Fengyang were thin and weak, so Naipu broadly memorialized requesting that Heilongjiang troops be transferred by way of Shandong and Jiangnan, proceeding directly to Anhui—far off they could extend a supporting voice to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and close at hand they could secure the gateways of Luzhou and Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Taiping rebels took Jiujiang, raided northern Anhui, and turned their gaze toward Beixiang. With Luzhou and Fengyang poorly defended, Naipu submitted a broad memorial asking that Heilongjiang troops be redeployed through Shandong and Jiangnan straight into Anhui—far away to lend strength to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and close by to hold the gates of Luzhou and Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 調刑部，尋擢工部尚書，調刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments; soon he was promoted to Minister of Works, then transferred again to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of Punishments, soon promoted to Minister of Works, and then transferred back to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 國子監司業崇福奏請豫徵山西咸豐四年錢糧，軍機大臣等會議，推及陝西、四川兩省，乃普偕侍郎何彤雲奏言：「各省情形不一，應由各督撫體察情形。

translations.literal: Chong Fu, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, memorialized requesting advance collection of Shanxi's tax grain for the fourth year of Xianfeng. The Grand Council and others deliberated and extended the matter to Shaanxi and Sichuan. Naipu, together with Vice Minister He Tongyun, memorialized, saying: "Conditions in the provinces are not uniform; each governor-general and governor should investigate local circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Fu, Vice Director of the Imperial Academy, asked to levy Shanxi's Xianfeng fourth-year taxes in advance. After the Grand Council extended the proposal to Shaanxi and Sichuan, Naipu and Vice Minister He Tongyun submitted that conditions differed from province to province and that each governor-general and governor should assess the situation on the ground.

sentences.zh: 山西被賊各州縣及陝西之延安、榆林、綏德、興安，四川之寧遠各府，地瘠民貧，均請免其借徵。

translations.literal: The counties in Shanxi overrun by bandits, and the prefectures of Yan'an, Yulin, Suide, and Xing'an in Shaanxi, and Ningyuan in Sichuan, all had barren land and impoverished people, and they all requested exemption from advance collection.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that advance collection be waived in Shanxi's bandit-ravaged counties, in Shaanxi's prefectures of Yan'an, Yulin, Suide, and Xing'an, and in Sichuan's Ningyuan—regions where the soil was poor and the people destitute.

sentences.zh: 至畸零小戶，有田數畝或數十畝，僅足餬口，仍令照常例完納，庶民力不至重困。」

translations.literal: As for scattered small households with only a few mu or several dozen mu of land, barely enough to feed themselves, they should still be required to pay according to the usual quota, so that the people's strength would not be heavily burdened."
translations.idiomatic: For scattered smallholders with only a few or a few dozen mu of land—barely enough to live on—they proposed that normal annual payments still be collected, so the common people would not be crushed under an even heavier load.

sentences.zh: 又奏言：「時值嚴寒，用兵尤宜撫卹。

translations.literal: They also memorialized, saying: "The season is bitterly cold, and in conducting military operations it is especially fitting to show care and relief.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "The weather is fiercely cold, and troops in the field above all need comfort and relief.

sentences.zh: 聞通永鎮兵四百名，去賊最近，而強半尚衣秋衣；

translations.literal: It is reported that of the four hundred soldiers at Tongyong garrison, who are closest to the rebels, more than half are still wearing autumn clothing;
translations.idiomatic: They had heard that of the four hundred men at Tongyong—the post nearest the enemy—more than half were still in autumn uniforms;

sentences.zh: 重以行營所在，百物昂貴，無錢者往往須取於民，以致負販裹足，兵士轉不免於飢寒。

translations.literal: Added to this, wherever the field camp is located, all goods are costly; those without money often have to take from the people, so that peddlers shrink back and dare not come, and the soldiers in turn cannot escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, wherever the camp moved, prices soared; men without cash often extorted the local people, peddlers stopped coming, and the soldiers themselves went hungry and cold.

sentences.zh: 請飭統兵大臣悉心籌度。」

translations.literal: They request that the commanding generals be ordered to plan this matter with full care."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that the field commanders be instructed to address the problem thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 又言：「江南大營老師糜餉，皆由琦善等意見不和，舒興阿自陝赴皖，所在稽留，沿途需索。

translations.literal: They also said: "The Jiangnan Grand Camp's long stalemate and wasted supplies are all due to the discord among Qishan and the others; Shu Xing'a, coming from Shaanxi to Anhui, delayed everywhere he went and made demands all along the route.
translations.idiomatic: They went on: "The Jiangnan Grand Camp's stalemate and wasted pay stem from the mutual distrust of Qishan and his colleagues. Shu Xing'a, sent from Shaanxi to Anhui, dawdled at every stop and requisitioned all along the road.

sentences.zh: 今命與江忠源會剿，不獨難以和衷，且恐因之掣肘。

translations.literal: Now that he has been ordered to join Jiang Zhongyuan in joint suppression, not only will it be hard to work in harmony, but there is also fear that they will hamper one another.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has been ordered to campaign jointly with Jiang Zhongyuan, they will not only find it hard to cooperate—they may well tie each other's hands.

sentences.zh: 又方今餉需艱難，軍務一日未蕆，即度支一日不敷，惟在大師刻日奏功，以紓天下之困。

translations.literal: Moreover, at present supplies are hard to come by; so long as military affairs are not concluded even for one day, the budget will fall short for one day. Only if the main armies can report victory day by day can the empire's distress be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: With supplies scarce, every day the war continued was another day the treasury could not keep up. Only swift victory by the main armies could ease the empire's strain.

sentences.zh: 請皇上嚴加督責，信賞必罰，以振暮氣。」

translations.literal: They request that Your Majesty strictly supervise and press them, rewarding the faithful and punishing without fail, in order to rouse stagnant morale.
translations.idiomatic: They urged the emperor to press his commanders hard, reward merit and punish failure without exception, and shake off the army's torpor.

sentences.zh: 疏上，嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and approved it warmly.

sentences.zh: 四年，刑部主事王式言坐承審命案，聽授請託，失入絞罪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wang Shiyan, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, was found guilty for presiding over a capital case, accepting entreaties, and wrongly imposing the sentence of strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Wang Shiyan, a principal clerk of the Ministry of Punishments, was convicted of hearing a capital case, taking improper requests, and wrongly sentencing the defendant to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上命裕誠等按治，乃普以式言本門生，奏請迴避，弗許。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor ordered Yucheng and others to investigate according to law. Naipu, because Shiyan had been his student, memorialized requesting recusal, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported, the emperor ordered Yucheng and others to investigate. Naipu, Shiyan's former teacher, asked to recuse himself, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 既而裕誠等讞式言僕受賕，上責乃普回護，降補內閣學士，罷直南書房。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yucheng and the others judged that Shiyan's servant had taken a bribe. The Emperor rebuked Naipu for shielding him, demoted him to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and removed him from duty in the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng's inquiry then found that Shiyan's servant had taken a bribe. The emperor blamed Naipu for covering for him, reduced him to a Grand Secretariat academician, and stripped him of his Southern Studio post.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部侍郎，擢​​左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of Rites and then promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，命督五城團防。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was ordered to supervise the militia defense of the Five Cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was put in charge of the Five Cities' militia defense.

sentences.zh: 九年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十年，文宗三旬慶辰，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, on the thirtieth birthday of the Wenzong Emperor, he was granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, on Emperor Wenzong's thirtieth birthday, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九月，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he pleaded illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，卒，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi, he died, and was given the posthumous title Wenkai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Tongzhi and was posthumously titled Wenkai.

sentences.zh: 子彭壽，字仁山。

translations.literal: His son was Peng Shou, courtesy name Renshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Peng Shou, styled Renshan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷少詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin probationer, appointed compiler, and was repeatedly promoted until he became Junior Commissioner of the Heir Apparent's Education.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Daoguang 27, he entered the Hanlin as a probationer, served as a compiler, and rose eventually to Junior Commissioner of the Heir Apparent's Education.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，文宗崩，命議郊配禮，彭壽偕大理寺少卿潘祖廕奏言：「臣讀大行皇帝聖制甲寅孟夏齋宮即事詩，末句'以後無須再變更'，注云：'天壇配享，三祖、五宗為定，永不增配位。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, when the Wenzong Emperor died, he was ordered to deliberate the rites of suburban sacrifice and paired offerings. Peng Shou, together with Pan Zuyin, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, memorialized, saying: "We have read the late Emperor's imperial composition, the poem On Affairs at the Fasting Palace in the First Month of Jiayin, whose final line reads, 'Thereafter there is no need for further change,' with a note stating: "Pairings at the Altar of Heaven are fixed at the Three Ancestors and Five Emperors; paired seats shall never be added.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11, after Emperor Wenzong's death, he was ordered to help settle the rites of suburban sacrifice and spirit-tablet pairing. Peng Shou and Pan Zuyin, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, cited the late emperor's poem composed at the fasting palace in the first month of Jiayin, whose closing line—"after this, let nothing be changed again"—was glossed: "Heaven Altar pairings are fixed at the Three Ancestors and Five Emperors; no paired seats are ever to be added.

sentences.zh: 恐後代無知故違，則儀文太繁。

translations.literal: We fear that later generations, unknowingly violating this in error, would make the ritual overly elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: They feared that later ages, forgetting this rule, would needlessly multiply the ritual.

sentences.zh: '臣等仰瞻聖藻，躬懸齋宮，言法行則，非博謙讓虛名。

translations.literal: We look up to the sacred writing, which hangs in the fasting palace itself; his words are law and his acts are the standard—this was not an empty show of modesty.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred text still hangs in the fasting palace; his word was law, not a gesture of false humility.

sentences.zh: 弓劍未寒，不忍頓生異議。」

translations.literal: His bow and sword are not yet cold; we cannot bear to raise sudden objections."
translations.idiomatic: His bow and sword are scarcely cold; we cannot bear to reopen the question now.

sentences.zh: 禮遂定。

translations.literal: The rites were thereupon fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The rites were settled accordingly.

sentences.zh: 時肅順等獲罪，彭壽請察治黨援，旨令指實。

translations.literal: At that time, when Sushun and others were condemned, Peng Shou requested that their factional associates be investigated and punished. An edict ordered him to specify facts.
translations.idiomatic: When Sushun and his circle fell, Peng Shou asked that their associates be investigated; the throne told him to name names and prove his charges.

sentences.zh: 奏言侍郎成琦，太僕寺卿德克津泰，候補京堂富績，侍郎劉昆、黃宗漢。

translations.literal: He memorialized, naming Vice Minister Cheng Qi; De Kejintai, Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Fu Ji, a candidate for a capital post; and Vice Ministers Liu Kun and Huang Zonghan.
translations.idiomatic: He named Vice Minister Cheng Qi, Court of the Imperial Stud Director De Kejintai, capital-office candidate Fu Ji, and Vice Ministers Liu Kun and Huang Zonghan.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「糾彈諸事，朕早有聞，特懲一儆百，力挽頹靡。

translations.literal: He received an edict saying: "On these matters of impeachment, I have long been informed. I punish one to warn a hundred and forcefully reverse decline and laxity.
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "These impeachments are no surprise to me. I punish one man to warn the rest and forcefully pull the court back from its slide into slackness.

sentences.zh: 此後不諮既往，諸臣亦毋以黨援陳奏，致啟訐陷。」

translations.literal: Henceforth I shall not inquire into what is past, and all officials likewise must not memorialize on factional associates, lest mutual accusation and entrapment be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter I will not rake up the past, and you officials must not use factional ties as grounds for memorials that invite mutual denunciation.

sentences.zh: 於是陳孚恩等譴黜有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Fu'en and others were censured and dismissed to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fu'en and others were then punished and removed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 彭壽又以載垣等隨事刻深，戶部五宇官錢案請再清釐，從之。

translations.literal: Peng Shou also submitted that, because Zaituan and others were harsh in every matter, the case of the Ministry of Revenue's five-character official funds should be reexamined and cleared up. This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shou also argued that Zaituan and his allies had been excessively severe, and asked for a fresh audit of the Ministry of Revenue's "five-character" official-funds case. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 同治初，再遷內閣學士，署禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, he was again promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and served concurrently as Acting Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he was again made a Grand Secretariat academician and acted as Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: =趙光=趙光，字蓉舫，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Zhao Guang, styled Rongfang, was a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang, courtesy name Rongfang, was from Kunming, Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin probationer, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a Compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中，轉光祿寺少卿，五遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary, then to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and after five promotions became Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor and supervising secretary, then as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and after five promotions became Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War and then transferred to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，奏陳時務，略言：「安民先察吏，州縣為親民之官，秩卑責重。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor acceded to the throne, he memorialized on affairs of state, saying in summary: "To pacify the people, one must first examine officials. The magistrates of prefectures and counties are the officials closest to the people; their rank is low but their responsibility is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor took the throne, Zhao Guang submitted a policy memorial arguing that to settle the people one must first judge the officials. Prefectural and county magistrates, though low in rank, bore the heaviest burden of governing the people directly.

sentences.zh: 捐例屢開，仕塗益雜。

translations.literal: Purchase offices have repeatedly been opened, and the path to office grows ever more mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Office-selling quotas had been opened again and again, filling the bureaucracy with unqualified men.

sentences.zh: 幕友招搖，書役播弄，賄囑情託，靡所不至。

translations.literal: Staff members swagger about, clerks manipulate affairs, and bribery, entreaty, and favoritism reach everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Private secretaries threw their weight around, yamen clerks twisted cases, and bribery and backdoor favor reached into every corner.

sentences.zh: 正供則挪移侵虧，訟案則株連擱壓，偶或參劾，輒籌抵制。

translations.literal: Regular tax payments are diverted, embezzled, and lost; in lawsuits people are implicated and cases shelved; if occasionally impeached, they at once scheme to resist.
translations.idiomatic: They diverted and embezzled regular tax payments, entangled litigants and shelved lawsuits, and whenever impeachment threatened, they organized to block it.

sentences.zh: 大吏慮其噬臍，曲予寬容，同僚相率效尤，成為習慣。

translations.literal: High officials, fearing that they may bite back, bend to indulgence; colleagues follow suit one after another, and this has become custom.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors, fearing retaliation, looked the other way; colleagues copied them until indulgence became habit.

sentences.zh: 應請飭令督、撫、司、道，嚴行舉錯，以肅官方。

translations.literal: It should be requested that governors-general, governors, provincial judges, and circuit intendants be ordered strictly to carry out promotion and dismissal, so as to rectify official discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that governors-general, governors, provincial judges, and circuit intendants be ordered to promote the worthy and remove the unfit, and so restore official discipline.

sentences.zh: 國家糜餉養兵，冀收實用，近日營伍將弁，虛文操演，廝役士卒，養尊處優。

translations.literal: The state wastes funds to maintain troops, hoping to obtain real use; recently, in the camps, officers and commanders have made a show of drill on paper, set servants to order soldiers about, and lived in comfort and privilege.
translations.idiomatic: The state poured out pay to maintain armies meant for real service, yet officers now treated drill as empty form, let servants boss the rank and file, and lived in ease and privilege.

sentences.zh: 空名漁利，器械不修，槍砲無準，而水師尤為窳敝。

translations.literal: They hold empty titles to fish for profit; weapons are not maintained, guns and cannon are inaccurate, and the navy is especially decayed and worn.
translations.idiomatic: They kept hollow ranks for profit while arms went unrepaired, muskets and cannon untested, and the navy rotted worst of all.

sentences.zh: 往往居岸自適，風沙水線，都未研習，洋面不靖，盜劫頻聞。

translations.literal: Often they stay ashore at their ease; wind, sand, and waterlines they have not studied at all. The seas are unsettled, and reports of piracy and robbery are frequently heard.
translations.idiomatic: They preferred the comfort of shore, never training in wind, shoals, or coastal waters; with the seas unsafe, piracy and robbery were reported constantly.

sentences.zh: 前者海疆有事，船遠距而彈施，敵近前而藥罄，束手無策，栗體先逃。

translations.literal: Previously, when the coast had trouble, ships fired while still far off, and when the enemy drew near the powder was already exhausted; helpless, they trembled and fled first.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble came before, ships opened fire from too far away, ran out of shot as the enemy closed, and then fled in panic with nothing left to do.

sentences.zh: 凡諸軍備，轉為寇齎。

translations.literal: All military stores in turn became provisions for bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, the empire's own stores supplied the raiders.

sentences.zh: 甚至軌律盡隳，沿途坐索，長官乞哀，乃始進行。

translations.literal: They even cast regulations aside entirely, sitting along the route to demand payment; only when superiors begged in supplication would they finally advance.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline collapsed so far that troops ignored every rule, extorted towns along the march, and moved on only after their commanders pleaded with them.

sentences.zh: 軍威不肅，一至於此。

translations.literal: Military authority was not maintained—matters had come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Military discipline had sunk to that level.

sentences.zh: 夫練兵必先練將，材藝邁眾，忠勇無前，如昔時楊遇春輩，渺不可得，緩急何恃？

translations.literal: Now, to train troops one must first train generals. Talents and skills surpassing the multitude, loyal and brave beyond compare, like Yang Yuchun and his kind in former times, are scarcely to be obtained—on whom can one rely in urgency?
translations.idiomatic: To train soldiers one must first train commanders, yet men of surpassing skill and fearless loyalty like Yang Yuchun were now almost impossible to find. In a crisis, whom could the state trust?

sentences.zh: 應請飭令將軍、督、撫、提、鎮，整齊營伍，鼓勵人才，以修武備。

translations.literal: It should be requested that generals, governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders be ordered to put the camps in order, encourage talent, and repair military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that generals, governors, provincial commanders, and garrison commanders be ordered to restore order in the camps, nurture capable men, and rebuild the armed forces.

sentences.zh: 詰姦除暴，莫如保甲，近來直隸、山東盜賊日眾，至河南之捻匪，四川之啯匪，廣東之土匪，貴州之苗匪，雲南之回匪，肆意強橫，目無法紀，邪教充斥，名目紛繁。

translations.literal: For investigating evil and suppressing violence, nothing is better than the baojia system. Recently bandits in Zhili and Shandong grow daily more numerous; as for the Nian bandits in Henan, the Gufei in Sichuan, the local bandits in Guangdong, the Miao bandits in Guizhou, and the Hui bandits in Yunnan, they act with reckless force, regard the law as nothing, heterodox sects fill the land, and their names and factions are many and confused.
translations.idiomatic: For rooting out crime, nothing matched the baojia system. Yet banditry was swelling in Zhili and Shandong, while Nian rebels in Henan, Gufei in Sichuan, local bandits in Guangdong, Miao rebels in Guizhou, and Hui rebels in Yunnan ran rampant, scorned the law, and multiplied under a tangle of sects and names.

sentences.zh: 煽誘既眾，蹂躪彌多。

translations.literal: As incitement and enticement grow widespread, devastation becomes ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: The more they recruited followers, the wider the destruction spread.

sentences.zh: 地方文武，恐滋事端，惟務姑息。

translations.literal: Local civil and military officials, fearing that trouble may arise, devote themselves only to indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Local civil and military officers, afraid of provoking incidents, chose only to appease.

sentences.zh: 胥差既豢賊縱容，兵弁復得規徇隱。

translations.literal: Runners and petty officers already feed bandits and connive at indulgence, while soldiers and officers in turn gain by covering for them.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen runners fed the bandits and looked the other way, while soldiers and petty officers profited by hiding them.

sentences.zh: 幹吏嚴拘，則聲息潛通，奪犯戕官，釀成巨患。

translations.literal: When capable officials strictly arrest them, word is secretly passed; prisoners are seized, officials are killed, and great calamity is brewed.
translations.idiomatic: When able officers tried to crack down, warnings leaked out; prisoners were rescued, officials murdered, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 其愚懦者，但期文過，諱盜為竊，避重就輕，以至匪徒益無忌憚，禍不勝言。

translations.literal: The foolish and timid merely seek to gloss over matters on paper, calling robbery theft and avoiding the serious to take the light, so that bandits grow ever more unafraid and the harm is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: The timid and incompetent merely papered over the record—calling robbery mere theft, choosing lesser charges over graver ones—until outlaws lost all fear and the harm became incalculable.

sentences.zh: 應請飭令各直省督撫，認真整頓，奉行保甲，緝捕勤能，據實獎勵；

translations.literal: It should be requested that the governors-general and governors of all provinces earnestly put matters in order, carry out the baojia system, and reward diligence and ability in arrest according to fact;
translations.idiomatic: He urged every provincial governor to enforce the baojia system in earnest and reward officials who pursued bandits diligently and effectively;

sentences.zh: 疲玩者撤參重處，以戢盜風。

translations.literal: Those who are slack and negligent should be dismissed and severely punished, so as to check the bandit wind.
translations.idiomatic: negligent ones should be removed and punished severely to curb the tide of banditry.

sentences.zh: 直省倉庫錢糧，各有定額，州縣官如果侭數徵解，交代清晰，何至虧空盈千累萬？

translations.literal: The treasuries and tax grain of the provinces each have fixed quotas. If magistrates of prefectures and counties fully collected and remitted the amounts and handed over accounts clearly, how could deficits mount to thousands and accumulate to tens of thousands?
translations.idiomatic: Every provincial treasury had fixed quotas. If magistrates collected and remitted in full and kept clear accounts on transfer, how could deficits pile into the thousands and tens of thousands?

sentences.zh: 其致此之由，厥有數端：或紈褲而登仕版，習尚奢華；

translations.literal: The reasons this comes about are several: some enter office as silk-trousered youths and are given to luxury.
translations.idiomatic: The causes were many: some took office as pampered youths addicted to display.

sentences.zh: 或庸瞶而暱親隨，開銷浮濫；

translations.literal: Some are mediocre and dull yet close to personal attendants, with reckless and excessive expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Some were mediocre men who favored personal cronies and spent recklessly.

sentences.zh: 或負累已深，官項償其私債；

translations.literal: Some are already deeply in debt and use public funds to repay private debts.
translations.idiomatic: Some were already deep in debt and used public money to pay private creditors.

sentences.zh: 或交游太廣，正款供其應酬。

translations.literal: Some have too wide a circle of acquaintances, and regular funds are spent on social obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Others kept too wide a social circle and spent official funds on entertainment and favors.

sentences.zh: 寅支卯糧，東挪西掩，有漕者藉口於幫丁之需索，解庫者歸咎於糧價之增昂。

translations.literal: They spend tomorrow's grain today, shifting funds east to cover west; those with grain transport use the demands of transport crews as a pretext, and those remitting to the treasury blame the rise in grain prices.
translations.idiomatic: They spent tomorrow's revenue today, robbing one account to patch another; grain-transport officials blamed transport crews' exactions, and remitting officers blamed rising grain prices.

sentences.zh: 道府察知，往往礙於情面，曲意彌縫，後任慮招重怨而不敢發，上司恐興大獄而不敢參，即使查抄，終歸無著。

translations.literal: When circuit intendants and prefects detect this, they often hindered by personal ties bend their intent to cover it up; successors fear inviting heavy resentment and dare not expose it; superiors fear raising a major case and dare not impeach; even if an investigation and seizure are made, in the end nothing is recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendants and prefects who learned of it often smoothed matters over for friends; successors feared bitter reprisals and kept silent; superiors feared major scandals and held back impeachments; even searches usually recovered nothing.

sentences.zh: 是以州縣交代，有歷數任而未算結者，有合數十州縣而未盤查者。

translations.literal: Thus in the handover of prefectural and county offices, there are some who pass through several terms without final reckoning, and some where several dozen prefectures and counties have never been audited.
translations.idiomatic: Hence magistrates sometimes served term after term without a settled account, and whole groups of counties went unaudited for years.

sentences.zh: 前者欽差大臣會同各督撫清查整理，嚴定章程，虧短各案，業已分別攤賠。

translations.literal: Previously, imperial commissioners together with the various governors-general cleared up and organized matters, strictly fixed regulations, and in each case of shortage the losses have already been separately apportioned for repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commissioners working with the governors had already audited the books, fixed new rules, and apportioned past shortages for repayment.

sentences.zh: 第恐舊虧未完，新虧已續，應請敕令各直省督撫督同司道各官詳細查覈，交代未清者，停其委署升補，虧那者嚴參，以清積弊。」

translations.literal: Only there is fear that old deficits not yet cleared will be followed by new ones already continuing. It should be requested that an edict order the governors-general and governors of all provinces to supervise the provincial and circuit officials in detailed examination and verification; those whose handovers are not cleared should have their acting appointments and promotions stopped, and those who embezzle and divert should be severely impeached, so as to clear accumulated abuses."
translations.idiomatic: But old deficits remained unsettled while new ones opened. He asked that governors supervise a thorough audit: officials with unsettled accounts should be barred from promotion or acting appointments, and embezzlers severely impeached, until the accumulated rot was cleared away.

sentences.zh: 疏入，優詔嘉納。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, a gracious edict praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial and commended it in a warm edict.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢工部尚書，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Minister of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 八年，命偕尚書周祖培等督五城團防事宜，歷兼署工部、兵部、戶部、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was ordered together with Minister Zhou Zupei and others to supervise the affairs of the Five Cities' militia defense, and he successively served concurrently as Acting Minister of Works, War, Revenue, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was ordered, together with Minister Zhou Zupei and others, to oversee the Five Cities' militia defense, and concurrently acted as Minister of Works, War, Revenue, and Personnel in turn.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he died, and was given the posthumous title Wenkai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died and was posthumously titled Wenkai.

sentences.zh: =硃嶟=硃嶟，字致堂，雲南通海人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zun, styled Zhitang, was a native of Tonghai in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zun, courtesy name Zhitang, was from Tonghai, Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十四年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin probationer, appointed proofreader, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, served as a proofreader, and was then made a censor.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年，畿輔災，廣東副貢生潘仕成捐貲助賑，賜舉人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang, when the capital region suffered disaster, Pan Shicheng of Guangdong, a stipend student, donated funds to aid relief and was granted the status of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Daoguang, when the capital region suffered famine, Pan Shicheng, a Guangdong stipend student, donated relief funds and was granted juren status.

sentences.zh: 有援案以請者，嶟疏言：「仕成本副貢，去舉人一間，賜以舉人，於破格之中，仍寓量才之意。

translations.literal: When others cited precedent to request the same, Zun memorialized, saying: "Shicheng was originally a stipend student, one step below a provincial graduate; to grant him graduate status, within an exceptional measure, still embodied the idea of measuring talent.
translations.idiomatic: When others cited his case to seek the same favor, Zhu Zun argued that Pan Shicheng, though only a stipend student one rank below juren, had been rewarded within an exceptional rule that still respected merit.

sentences.zh: 厥後葉元堃、黃立誠次第援請，若因此遂成定例，生富人徼幸，阻寒士進修，於事不便。

translations.literal: Afterward Ye Yuanjun and Huang Licheng successively cited precedent to request the same. If because of this it should become a fixed precedent, wealthy men would seize their chance, obstruct poor scholars in advancing their studies, and this would be inconvenient to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ye Yuanjun and Huang Licheng invoked the same precedent. If that became standard practice, rich men would chase windfalls and block poor scholars from advancement.

sentences.zh: 應請旨飭各督撫，水旱偏災，捐輸應獎，不得援引前案。」

translations.literal: It should be requested that an edict order the various governors-general and governors that, in cases of flood, drought, and partial disaster, donations may be rewarded, but prior cases must not be cited.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that governors be instructed: after floods, droughts, or localized disasters, donors might still be rewarded, but no one should cite earlier cases as precedent.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 五遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he became Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢兵部侍郎，迭兼署吏、戶二部，坐事鐫五秩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and successively served concurrently as Acting Minister of Personnel and Revenue; for an offense he was reduced five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made Vice Minister of War and concurrently acted as Minister of Personnel and Revenue; later he was demoted five ranks for an offense.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，補內閣侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was restored as Reader of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was restored as a Reader of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 御史劉良駒條奏銀錢畫一，上命各省督撫議奏。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Liangju submitted a detailed memorial on unifying silver and copper cash. The Emperor ordered the governors-general and governors of the provinces to deliberate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Liangju memorialized on unifying silver and copper currency, and the emperor ordered the provincial governors to study the question and reply.

sentences.zh: 嶟疏言：「泉布之寶，國專其利，故定賦以粟，而平貨以錢。

translations.literal: Zun memorialized, saying: "The treasure of coin and cloth is a profit monopolized by the state; therefore taxes are fixed in grain, and goods are balanced by money.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zun replied that coinage was a state monopoly: taxes were assessed in grain, while commerce was settled in cash.

sentences.zh: 物賤由乎錢少，少則重，重則加鑄而散之使輕；

translations.literal: When goods are cheap, it is because money is scarce; when scarce, it is heavy; when heavy, more is cast and dispersed to make it light;
translations.idiomatic: When goods were cheap, money was scarce; scarcity made it heavy, and the state responded by minting more to lighten it;

sentences.zh: 物貴由乎錢多，多則輕，輕則作法而斂之使重。

translations.literal: when goods are dear, it is because money is abundant; when abundant, it is light; when light, measures are devised to gather it in and make it heavy.
translations.idiomatic: when goods were dear, money was plentiful; abundance made it light, and the state devised means to draw it in and restore weight.

sentences.zh: 一輕一重，張弛在官，而權操於上。

translations.literal: One light and one heavy—the tightening and loosening lie with the officials, but the power is held by the throne above.
translations.idiomatic: Light and heavy, tight and loose—the officials administered the cycle, but authority rested with the throne.

sentences.zh: 今出納以銀，錢幾置諸無用。

translations.literal: Now receipts and payments are made in silver, and cash is nearly placed among things of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Now receipts and payments ran in silver, and copper cash was all but abandoned.

sentences.zh: 雖國寶流通，然流於下而不轉於上。

translations.literal: Although the state's treasure circulates, it flows downward and does not return upward.
translations.idiomatic: Though currency still moved through the economy, it flowed down to the people and did not circulate back to the state.

sentences.zh: 於是富商市儈，得乘其乏、操其贏，而任意以為輕重。

translations.literal: Thereupon rich merchants and market brokers, able to exploit its scarcity and control its profit, arbitrarily made it light or heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Rich merchants and brokers then exploited shortages, controlled the spread, and set the value of money as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 若使官為定價，且必格而不行。

translations.literal: If the government were to fix prices, it would certainly fail to be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the state fixed prices, he warned, the rule would not hold.

sentences.zh: 要在因其便使人易從，通其變使人不怨，行其權使人不疑。

translations.literal: The key lies in following their convenience so that people readily comply, accommodating change so that people do not resent it, and exercising discretion so that people do not doubt it.
translations.idiomatic: The art was to follow what people found convenient so they would comply readily, allow for change so they would not resent it, and exercise discretion so they would not doubt the policy.

sentences.zh: 方今鹽務疲敝，皆以銀貴錢賤為詞，以鹽賣錢而不賣銀也。

translations.literal: At present the salt administration is exhausted and debilitated; all cite dear silver and cheap cash as their reason—that salt is sold for cash and not for silver.
translations.idiomatic: The salt administration was now in distress, and all blamed dear silver and cheap cash: salt was sold for copper, not silver.

sentences.zh: 賣錢即解錢，人必樂從，長蘆鹽價可解京充餉。

translations.literal: If sold for cash, the cash is immediately remitted; people will surely gladly comply, and Changlu salt revenues can be remitted to the capital for rations.
translations.idiomatic: Sell for cash and remit the cash at once—people would gladly comply, and Changlu salt revenues could be sent to the capital for pay.

sentences.zh: 請於東西城建庫藏錢，以戶、工左右侍郎掌之，按時價搭放各旗，就近赴庫請領，以免其轉運，並嚴禁剋扣、短陌、攙雜諸弊。

translations.literal: It is requested that treasuries for storing cash be built in the Eastern and Western Cities, managed by the Left and Right Vice Ministers of Revenue and of Works; disburse to each banner according to market price, with troops drawing from nearby treasuries to avoid transport, and strictly prohibit skimming, short counts, adulteration, and like abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed cash treasuries in the Eastern and Western Cities under the Left and Right Vice Ministers of Revenue and Works, disbursing to each banner at market rates so troops could draw nearby and avoid transport costs, with strict bans on skimming, short counts, adulteration, and like abuses.

sentences.zh: 兩淮鹽價，解備河工歲修。

translations.literal: Liang Huai salt revenues are remitted to supply annual river-works repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Huai salt revenues were remitted to fund annual river conservancy.

sentences.zh: 淮上全工，水路皆通，輓運較易，工次僱夫購料，俱系用錢，此兩便之道也。

translations.literal: All river works on the Huai are complete, waterways are open throughout, transport by cart is comparatively easy, and hiring labor and purchasing materials at each work site all require cash—this is the path of double convenience.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huai all works were complete and waterways open, so cart transport was easy and labor and materials were paid in cash—a double advantage.

sentences.zh: 農民以錢輸賦，天下十居七八。

translations.literal: Farmers pay taxes in cash; throughout the empire they comprise seven or eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers paid taxes in copper cash; they made up seven or eight tenths of the empire.

sentences.zh: 地方官收錢解銀，每致賠累。

translations.literal: When local officials collect cash and remit silver, they often incur losses to make up shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials collected cash and remitted silver, they often suffered losses.

sentences.zh: 江西撫臣吳文鎔前奏：'本省坐支之項，收錢放錢；

translations.literal: The Jiangxi governor Wu Wenrong previously memorialized: 'For items retained for local expenditure in this province, collect cash and disburse cash;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Governor Wu Wenrong had earlier argued: 'For items retained locally, collect and disburse cash;

sentences.zh: 解部候撥之款，徵銀解銀；

translations.literal: for funds remitted to the ministry awaiting allocation, levy silver and remit silver;
translations.idiomatic: for funds remitted to the ministry pending allocation, levy and remit silver;
