sentences.zh: 兵餉役食，請照時價改折。

translations.literal: for military pay and corvée rations, request conversion at market price.
translations.idiomatic: for military pay and corvée rations, convert at market rates.

sentences.zh: '其言不為無見。

translations.literal: His words were not without insight.
translations.idiomatic: There was merit in what he said.

sentences.zh: 惟全行收錢，往返搬運，倍增勞費。

translations.literal: Yet if cash alone were collected throughout, the back-and-forth transport would double labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Yet collecting cash alone everywhere would double the labor and cost of transport back and forth.

sentences.zh: 通省絕無銀幣，亦未免偏枯。

translations.literal: If the whole province had no silver currency at all, that too would unavoidably be one-sided.
translations.idiomatic: A province with no silver at all would likewise be lopsided.

sentences.zh: 擬請州縣徵收，向來徵銀解銀者置無論，但照現在收錢者，量錢糧多少，視附近地方兵役眾寡，酌減應解銀數，以紓其困。

translations.literal: It is proposed that in collection by prefectures and counties, those who have always levied silver and remitted silver be left aside; but for those now collecting cash, according to the amount of cash grain, considering how many or few soldiers and corvée laborers are nearby, reduce the amount of silver due for remission as appropriate to relieve their distress.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that counties still levying and remitting silver be left as they were, but where cash was already collected, the silver due for remission be reduced according to tax volume and the number of nearby troops and corvée laborers, to ease local hardship.

sentences.zh: 除易銀解司之外，即以錢抵銀，每銀一兩，折錢若干，酌定數目，按照時價，支放兵餉役食。

translations.literal: Apart from what is exchanged for silver and remitted to the provincial treasury, use cash in lieu of silver: for each tael of silver, convert to a fixed number of cash at market price to pay military rations and corvée provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond what was exchanged for silver and sent to the provincial treasury, cash would stand in for silver at a fixed rate per tael, paid at market price for military and corvée rations.

sentences.zh: 應有耗羨平餘，仍行提出解司，而本管同城之官俸，本州縣之書工、役食、祭祀、驛站，本地方分汛之兵餉，俱準坐支。

translations.literal: Wastage, surplus, and balancing remainder should still be submitted to the provincial treasury; but salaries of officials in the same city, clerks and corvée rations of the prefecture and county, sacrifices, post stations, and military pay for local garrisons may all be retained for local expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Wastage and surplus would still go to the provincial treasury, but salaries of city officials, county clerks and corvée rations, sacrifices, post stations, and local garrison pay would all be retained locally.

sentences.zh: 餘則視道路之遠近，解存道、府、籓各庫，以放兵餉。

translations.literal: The remainder, according to distance of the route, is remitted and stored in circuit, prefectural, and provincial treasuries for disbursing military pay.
translations.idiomatic: The rest would be deposited in circuit, prefectural, or provincial treasuries according to distance, for military pay.

sentences.zh: 時價則視省垣為準，以開徵前十日為定，由籓司通飭遵照，半年一更。

translations.literal: Market price shall take the provincial capital as standard, fixed ten days before collection opens, communicated and enforced by the provincial treasurer, revised every half year.
translations.idiomatic: Market rates would be set by the provincial capital, fixed ten days before collection opened, announced by the provincial treasurer, and revised every six months.

sentences.zh: 餉銀每兩折錢多不過千七百，少不過千二百，取為定則，不得再減。

translations.literal: For military pay, each tael of silver converted to cash shall be no more than 1,700 and no less than 1,200, taken as the fixed rule, and may not be reduced further.
translations.idiomatic: Military pay would convert each tael of silver to no more than 1,700 and no less than 1,200 cash—a fixed rule that could not be cut further.

sentences.zh: 至文武官廉俸無可坐支者，兵丁屯駐之區，附近州縣無收錢者，皆發銀如故。

translations.literal: As for civil and military salaries with nothing to retain locally, districts where soldiers are garrisoned but nearby counties collect no cash, and all such cases—silver shall be disbursed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military salaries that could not be retained locally, garrison districts where nearby counties collected no cash—all would still receive silver as before.

sentences.zh: 官局錢搭放向有成例者亦如故。

translations.literal: Existing precedents for disbursing cash from government offices shall also remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Existing rules for government cash disbursement would also stand.

sentences.zh: 如是，則雖變而實因，不至糾紛窒礙。

translations.literal: Thus, though there is change, in substance there is continuity, and disputes and obstruction will not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, though the form changed, the substance continued, and wrangling and deadlock would be avoided.

sentences.zh: 至如百姓出粟米麻絲易錢輸賦，久已習為故常，向收若干，今折若干，凡自封投櫃者，不遽改折，是於民無擾也。

translations.literal: As for common people who bring grain, millet, hemp, and silk to exchange for cash to pay taxes—a practice long customary—what was formerly collected in kind, now converted in fixed amounts: for those who seal and submit to the tax counter, do not abruptly change the conversion, and the people will not be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Where peasants had long exchanged grain, hemp, and silk for cash to pay taxes, those who sealed payment at the counter would not face abrupt conversion changes—no disturbance to the people.

sentences.zh: 兵丁領銀，仍須易錢然後適用。

translations.literal: When soldiers receive silver, they must still exchange it for cash before it can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who received silver still had to exchange it for cash before they could spend it.

sentences.zh: 每至兵領餉時，不准鋪戶抑價，今照定價放給滿錢，此於兵無虧也。

translations.literal: Whenever soldiers draw pay, shops must not be allowed to depress the price; now disburse full-weight cash at the fixed rate—this does soldiers no harm.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers drew pay, shops would no longer be allowed to undercut the rate; they would receive full-weight cash at the fixed price—no loss to the troops.

sentences.zh: 先時銀多，則官以收錢漁利；

translations.literal: Formerly, when silver was abundant, officials profited by collecting cash;
translations.idiomatic: When silver had been plentiful, officials profited by collecting cash;

sentences.zh: 今時錢賤，則官以易錢賠累。

translations.literal: now, when cash is cheap, officials suffer losses by exchanging for cash.
translations.idiomatic: now, with cash cheap, officials lost money exchanging for it.

sentences.zh: 多用錢則少解銀，即累亦因而減，迨銀價平時，又復​​可獲羨餘，此於官有益也。

translations.literal: Using more cash means remitting less silver; even losses are thereby reduced, and when the price of silver levels, surplus may again be gained—this benefits officials.
translations.idiomatic: More cash meant less silver remitted, reducing losses; when silver prices stabilized, surplus could be recovered—this benefited officials.

sentences.zh: 或謂錢收於上，則廛市一空，恐致錢荒。

translations.literal: Some say that if cash is collected upward, the markets will be emptied and cash scarcity may result.
translations.idiomatic: Some warned that collecting cash into government treasuries would drain the markets and cause a cash shortage.

sentences.zh: 不知兵役領錢，仍行於市，地方官除存庫外，尚有大半必須易銀解司，則其錢亦行於市。

translations.literal: They do not understand that when soldiers and corvée laborers receive cash, it still circulates in the market; apart from what local officials store in treasuries, more than half must still be exchanged for silver and remitted to the provincial treasury—so that cash also circulates in the market.
translations.idiomatic: But troops and corvée laborers paid in cash would still spend it in the market, and local officials, beyond what they kept on hand, would still exchange most of it for silver to remit upward—so cash would still circulate.

sentences.zh: 且今日之弊，不在錢荒而在錢濫，欲救其弊，莫利於收錢，尤莫利於停鑄。

translations.literal: Moreover, today's evil lies not in cash scarcity but in cash debasement; to remedy the evil, nothing is more beneficial than collecting cash, and nothing more beneficial than halting minting.
translations.idiomatic: Today's problem was not too little cash but too much debased cash; the best remedy was to collect cash—and above all to halt minting.

sentences.zh: 當此錢賤之時，暫停鼓鑄，以工本之銀，發出易錢，實收上庫。

translations.literal: At this time when cash is cheap, temporarily halt minting; use the silver of production cost, send it out to exchange for cash, and actually collect it into the upper treasury.
translations.idiomatic: While cash was cheap, minting should pause; production-cost silver would be sent out to buy cash back into the state treasury.

sentences.zh: 薄小者汰之，則私鑄難行，而官錢日多，錢價可平，而制錢一千準銀一兩之例，可得而行矣。

translations.literal: Reject thin and small coins, and private casting will be hard to practice; official cash will daily increase, the price of cash can level, and the rule that 1,000 standard cash equals one tael of silver can be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Reject thin, undersized coins and private casting would fail; official cash would grow, prices would stabilize, and the rule of one thousand standard cash per tael of silver could hold.

sentences.zh: 是知停鑄者用錢之轉關，平價者絕私之微權也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that halting minting is the turning point in using cash, and leveling prices is cutting off the petty power of private casters.
translations.idiomatic: Halting minting was the pivot of cash policy; leveling prices meant stripping private casters of their petty leverage.

sentences.zh: 將欲平價，非使銀錢相埒不可，為平價而暫停鑄，迨價平而復開爐，所謂欲贏先縮，一張一弛之道也。

translations.literal: To level prices, silver and cash must be made equal; to level prices, minting is temporarily halted, and when prices level, the furnaces reopen—this is what is meant by 'to gain, first contract,' the way of tension and release.
translations.idiomatic: To stabilize prices, silver and cash had to reach parity; minting would pause until they did, then resume—a case of contracting before expanding, tightening before loosening.

sentences.zh: 夫損上必期益下，今錢值日賤，物價日貴，泉府費兩錢而成一錢，官兵領一錢則僅當半錢。

translations.literal: Harm to the upper must be expected to benefit the lower; now the value of cash daily falls and the price of goods daily rises—the treasury spends two cash to make one, and when officers and soldiers receive one cash it is worth only half.
translations.idiomatic: What harmed the state should benefit the people—but cash fell daily while prices rose; the mint spent two coins to make one, and troops received coins worth only half their face value.

sentences.zh: 無益於民，有損於國，孰得孰失，必有能辨之者。

translations.literal: No benefit to the people, harm to the state—who gains and who loses, there must be those who can distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: The people gained nothing; the state lost. Anyone could see which side bore the cost.

sentences.zh: 總之可用錢則用錢，必須用銀則仍用銀。

translations.literal: In sum, use cash where cash may be used; where silver must be used, still use silver.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: use cash where cash would serve; use silver where silver was required.

sentences.zh: 附近則用錢，致遠則用銀。

translations.literal: Use cash nearby; use silver for distant transport.
translations.idiomatic: Cash for what was near; silver for what was far.

sentences.zh: 子母相權，贏縮有制，補偏救弊，無逾於此。

translations.literal: Principal and subsidiary balanced against each other, expansion and contraction regulated— to remedy bias and cure abuses, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Principal and subsidiary currencies in balance, expansion and contraction under control—no better way to correct bias and cure abuse.

sentences.zh: 惟各省情形不一，因地制宜，隨時變通。

translations.literal: Only each province's circumstances differ; adapt to local conditions and adjust as times require.
translations.idiomatic: Each province differed; policy should follow local conditions and change with the times.

sentences.zh: 當責各督撫體察酌議盡善。」

translations.literal: The various governors-general and governors should be charged to investigate, deliberate, and devise the best measures."
translations.idiomatic: Governors should be charged to investigate local conditions and devise the best measures.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上命軍機大臣會同戶部議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor ordered the Grand Council ministers jointly with the Ministry of Revenue to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor ordered the Grand Council and the Ministry of Revenue to study it and act.

sentences.zh: 歷通政副使、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Commissioner of the Transmission Office and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Commissioner of the Transmission Office and as a Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of Granary Storage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Granary Storage.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，病，乞罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, he fell ill and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he fell ill and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 五年，病痊，复授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when his illness healed, he was again appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, recovered from illness, he was again made Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 迭署兵、禮二部尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively in acting capacity as Minister of War and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Acting Minister of War and Acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, again on grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again fell ill and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，卒，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he died and was given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he died and was posthumously titled Wenduan.

sentences.zh: =李菡=李菡，字豐垣，順天寶坻人。

translations.literal: Li Han, styled Fengyuan, was a native of Baodi in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, courtesy name Fengyuan, was from Baodi, Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin probationer, and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍講，大考二等，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: After further promotion to Lecturer, he earned the second grade in the triennial evaluation and was made Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Lecturer, he earned the second grade in the triennial evaluation and was made Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷少詹事，督安徽學政，累遷通政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Junior Sub-Reader, served as Educational Commissioner of Anhui, and was promoted in succession to Transmission Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he became Junior Sub-Reader, served as Educational Commissioner of Anhui, and rose in turn to Transmission Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，署禮部侍郎，應詔上疏：「請戒飭諸臣：一曰振因循。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, acting as Vice Minister of Rites, he responded to an imperial edict with a memorial: "I beg that Your Majesty admonish the officials: first, rouse them from routine inertia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng, as Acting Vice Minister of Rites, he answered an imperial edict with a memorial: "I urge Your Majesty to admonish the officials. First, shake off routine inertia.

sentences.zh: 積習相仍，中外一轍。

translations.literal: Stale custom continues unbroken; court and provinces follow one track.
translations.idiomatic: Stale habits persisted; court and provinces marched in lockstep.

sentences.zh: 用兵無可退之理，乃引疾歸田，抽身保位，則因循在軍旅矣。

translations.literal: When war brooks no retreat, yet officers plead illness and retire to their fields, withdrawing to preserve their posts—then inertia lies in the armies.
translations.idiomatic: War brooked no retreat, yet officers pleaded illness, retired to their estates, and slipped away to save their posts—inertia had infected the armies.

sentences.zh: 治水為難緩之功，乃自冬徂夏，漫口未合，則因循在河防矣。

translations.literal: River control is work that cannot be postponed; yet from winter to summer the breach remained unclosed—then inertia lies in river defense.
translations.idiomatic: River works could not wait, yet from winter through summer the breach stayed open—inertia had infected flood control.

sentences.zh: 雍沙番案，琦善以總督大員，猶复語多狡飾，以至往返鞫訊，則因循在刑法矣。

translations.literal: In the Yongsha barbarian case, even Qishan as governor-general still spoke with much cunning evasion, so that inquiry went back and forth—then inertia lies in criminal law.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongsha border case, even Governor-General Qishan hedged and evaded until hearings dragged on—inertia had infected the law.

sentences.zh: 順天武清縣逃犯，竟敢窩藏匪徒，浙江奉化縣刁民並敢迫脅官長，則因循又在郡縣矣。

translations.literal: In Shuntian's Wuqing County a fugitive dared harbor bandits; in Zhejiang's Fenghua County unruly commoners dared even coerce their magistrate—then inertia lies in the prefectures and counties as well.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuqing, Shuntian, a fugitive dared shelter bandits; in Fenghua, Zhejiang, rowdies dared coerce their magistrate—inertia had reached the counties too.

sentences.zh: 伏原皇上乾綱獨振，力挽頹風，聞嘉謨則立見施行，睹弊政則悉除支蔓。

translations.literal: I bow and pray that Your Majesty alone revive the imperial authority, forcefully reverse the declining wind, hear good counsel and immediately put it into practice, and upon seeing faulty policy cut away all its tangled branches.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty alone stiffen the imperial will, reverse the slide, act on good counsel at once, and cut faulty policy to the root.

sentences.zh: 惰者責之，勇者獎之，勤者進之，昏者黜之，庶奮庸熙載，百廢俱修矣。

translations.literal: Reprove the idle, reward the brave, advance the diligent, remove the dull—then perhaps all will strive in their posts and every neglected task be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Punish the slack, reward the bold, promote the diligent, dismiss the dull—then every neglected office might stir again.

sentences.zh: 一曰除欺飾。

translations.literal: Second, remove deception and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Second, end deception and cover-ups.

sentences.zh: 粵西逆匪，萌蘗在十數年之前，使撫臣早為奏聞，何難根株立絕？

translations.literal: The Guangxi rebels sprouted more than ten years ago; had the governor reported early, how hard would it have been to uproot them at once?
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi rebels had been sprouting for more than a decade; had the governor reported early, they could have been uprooted at once.

sentences.zh: 乃養癰成患，諱莫如深。

translations.literal: Instead they nurtured an abscess into a calamity and concealed it beyond all depth.
translations.idiomatic: Instead officials nursed the sore into a plague and buried the truth.

sentences.zh: 比及有人指陳，勢已不可撲滅。

translations.literal: By the time someone pointed it out, the situation could no longer be stamped out.
translations.idiomatic: By the time anyone spoke up, the fire could no longer be stamped out.

sentences.zh: 年來勞師糜餉，迄無成功，禍首罪魁，實由欺始。

translations.literal: Years of armies exhausted and funds squandered, with no success to the end—the chief culprit and source of disaster truly began with deception.
translations.idiomatic: Years of armies exhausted and treasury drained, with nothing won—the chief culprit was deception from the start.

sentences.zh: 夫獻可替否，宰相之責也；

translations.literal: To offer what is acceptable and replace what is not is the duty of the chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: To offer what works and replace what fails is the prime minister's duty;

sentences.zh: 拾遺補闕，諫官之職也。

translations.literal: to gather what is missing and mend what is lacking is the office of the remonstrating censor.
translations.idiomatic: to gather omissions and mend gaps is the censor's office.

sentences.zh: 伏望皇上開誠佈公，虛懷善納，導之使言，言之使盡，執兩用中，歸於至當。

translations.literal: I bow and hope Your Majesty will open your heart with sincerity, hold an open mind and welcome good counsel, lead men to speak and let them speak fully, hold to the mean between two extremes, and arrive at what is most fitting.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty speak plainly, listen openly, draw men out until they have said all they mean, hold the mean, and arrive at what is right.

sentences.zh: 至科道職司言責，尤朝廷耳目之官，風聞偶誤，小過可容，庶贛直得效其愚，萋菲莫行其罔，而宸聰四達矣。

translations.literal: As for the censorate, charged with the duty of speech and especially the eyes and ears of the court—if rumor occasionally errs, small faults may be forgiven, so that honest bluntness may serve its foolish loyalty and slander may not practice its deceit, and the imperial hearing may reach everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate bears the duty of speech and serves as the court's eyes and ears; if rumor errs, small faults may pass, so blunt honesty can do its work and slander cannot deceive—and the throne will hear in every direction.

sentences.zh: 一曰屏偏私。

translations.literal: Third, banish partiality and private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Third, banish faction and private interest.

sentences.zh: 人之氣質，不能無偏，意見少有參差，議論遂多齟《齒吾》。

translations.literal: Human temperament cannot be without bias; when opinions differ slightly, debate soon grows full of friction.
translations.idiomatic: No temperament is without bias; slight differences of view soon breed friction in debate.

sentences.zh: 相持不下，教令紛更，屬員既無所適從，宵小遂從而讒構。

translations.literal: When neither side yields, orders change in confusion; subordinates know not which to follow, and petty men take the chance to slander and intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: Deadlock breeds shifting orders; subordinates no longer know whom to obey, and petty men seize the chance to slander and plot.

sentences.zh: 嫌隙日深，乖氣致戾。

translations.literal: Resentment deepens day by day; perverse qi breeds calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment deepens; ill will breeds disaster.

sentences.zh: 刑部越獄一事，非其明驗乎？

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments prison-break—is that not clear proof?
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments prison break—is that not proof enough?

sentences.zh: 夫師克在和不在眾，兩粵會剿，湖南防堵，將帥不應有諉罪爭功之見，督撫不可存此疆爾界之私，同德同心，群策效力。

translations.literal: For an army, victory lies in harmony, not numbers. In the joint campaigns of the two Guang provinces and Hunan's blocking defense, generals must not shift blame or fight for credit; governors must not cherish territorial boundaries as their private interest—unite in virtue and purpose, and pool strength.
translations.idiomatic: Victory lies in harmony, not numbers. In joint campaigns in Guangdong, Guangxi, and Hunan, generals must not trade blame or vie for credit, nor governors guard petty boundaries—unite in purpose and pool strength.

sentences.zh: 苟無隙之可乘，定膚功之克奏。

translations.literal: If no gap can be exploited, certain victory will be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Leave no gap for the enemy, and victory will follow.

sentences.zh: 河、漕本屬一體，未有河不治而漕治者。

translations.literal: Rivers and grain transport are fundamentally one body; never has transport thrived while rivers were neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and the grain transport are one system; transport cannot thrive while rivers are neglected.

sentences.zh: 從前督臣、漕臣，曾因參劾廳員，各執己見，現在漫口不能合龍，漕船何由利濟？

translations.literal: Formerly the river governor and transport commissioner, having impeached an agency official, each clung to his own view; now the breach cannot be closed and grain boats cannot pass—how can transport prosper?
translations.idiomatic: River and transport commissioners once impeached an agency officer and each clung to his view; now the breach will not close and grain boats cannot pass—how can transport prosper?

sentences.zh: 億萬姓饑民待賑，數百萬帑項虛糜，正大臣憂患與共之時。

translations.literal: Tens of millions of starving people await relief; millions in treasury funds are wasted in vain—this is precisely when great ministers should share the nation's woes.
translations.idiomatic: Millions starve awaiting relief; millions in treasury funds are wasted—this is when great ministers should share the nation's burden.

sentences.zh: 此即屏除嫌怨，共秉公忠，猶恐難以濟時屯而紓民患；

translations.literal: Even if they cast aside resentment and joined in loyal fairness, one still fears it would be hard to meet the crisis and ease the people's suffering;
translations.idiomatic: Even if they set aside grudges and acted in loyal concert, it might still be hard to meet the crisis and ease the people's pain;

sentences.zh: 倘仍芥蒂未化，籌畫分歧，不和政龐，咎將誰執？

translations.literal: if grudges remain unsettled, plans diverge, and discord thickens policy—who will bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: if grudges linger and plans diverge, who will answer when policy fails?

sentences.zh: 伏讀仁宗御製和同論，諄諄以臣下偏私為戒。

translations.literal: I bow and read the Renzong Emperor's imperial essay "On Harmony," earnestly warning against officials' partiality.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the Renzong Emperor's essay On Harmony, which earnestly warns officials against partiality.

sentences.zh: 原皇上一德交孚，與百僚共襄上理焉。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty unite in virtue with all officials and together uphold good governance.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty unite in virtue with all officials and govern as one.

sentences.zh: 一曰防玩法。

translations.literal: Fourth, guard against lax enforcement of rules.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, guard against lax regard for law.

sentences.zh: 現今軍務、河工，貽誤諸臣，厥咎匪細。

translations.literal: In present military affairs and river works, the officials who have caused delay bear no small fault.
translations.idiomatic: In military affairs and river works today, those who have caused delay bear no small blame.

sentences.zh: 仰蒙寬典，僅予薄懲，恕其既往之愆，責其將來之報。

translations.literal: By imperial grace they received only light punishment, their past faults forgiven, their future service demanded.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial grace they received only light punishment—past faults forgiven, future service required.

sentences.zh: 而且失伍之將弁，准其帶罪立功，潰防之河員，許其留工效力，恢宏大度，格外矜全，天下皆曉然於聖人不得已之苦心，與夫通變權宜之計，該大臣等久蒙倚任，渥荷優容，自無不激厲圖功，竭忠矢志。

translations.literal: Moreover, officers who had lost formation were allowed to redeem themselves through merit, river officials who had let dikes fail were permitted to remain at their posts—magnanimity beyond measure, favor beyond ordinary. All the realm understood the sage's reluctant heart and his expedient measures; these great ministers, long trusted and richly favored, could hardly fail to rouse themselves, strive for merit, and devote themselves utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted officers were allowed to redeem themselves in battle; failed river officials were kept on the works—grace beyond measure. The empire understood the emperor's reluctant heart and his expedient mercy; these long-favored ministers could hardly fail to rouse themselves and serve with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 第恐奔走禦侮，難得賢員，幸澤恃恩，復萌故智。

translations.literal: I only fear that in rushing to repel invaders worthy men are hard to find, while those who profit from favor rely on indulgence and revive their old tricks.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that in the rush to defend the realm worthy men are scarce, while the favored rely on indulgence and fall back on old habits.

sentences.zh: 始猶懼罪之不可逭，一旦獲宥，遂謂罪有可原矣；

translations.literal: At first they still feared punishment could not be escaped; once pardoned, they conclude their guilt may be excused;
translations.idiomatic: At first they still feared guilt could not be escaped; once pardoned, they decide guilt can be forgiven;

sentences.zh: 初猶慮法之不能逃，幸而苟免，遂謂法止於是矣。

translations.literal: at first they still worried the law could not be evaded; having narrowly escaped, they conclude the law goes no further.
translations.idiomatic: at first they still feared the law could not be dodged; having narrowly escaped, they decide the law stops here.

sentences.zh: 伏原皇上奮天錫之勇，播神武之風，寬大之詔，能發而即能收，希冀之恩，可一而不可再。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will summon heaven-given courage and spread divine martial bearing: a decree of generosity can be issued and also withdrawn; favor hoped for may be given once, not twice.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty summon heaven-given courage and show divine martial bearing: a decree of mercy can be issued and withdrawn; favor hoped for may be granted once, not twice.

sentences.zh: 則德威惟畏，玩縱之萌，不戢自止矣。

translations.literal: Then virtue and awe alike will inspire fear, and the sprout of lax indulgence will cease without being curbed.
translations.idiomatic: Then virtue and awe together will inspire fear, and lax indulgence will die unbidden.

sentences.zh: 以上四條，皆臣道之防，實切時之弊，而其本由於得人。

translations.literal: The four points above are all bulwarks of ministerial duty, truly cutting to present evils—and their root lies in getting the right men.
translations.idiomatic: These four points guard ministerial duty and cut to present evils; their root is getting the right men.

sentences.zh: 進英銳，則因循者退矣；

translations.literal: Advance the sharp and keen, and the routine-bound will withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: Promote the sharp and keen, and the routine-bound will fall away;

sentences.zh: 取誠篤，則欺飾者鮮矣。

translations.literal: choose the sincere and honest, and deceivers will be few.
translations.idiomatic: choose the sincere and honest, and deceivers will grow rare.

sentences.zh: 惟在皇上任賢勿疑，用材器使，俾朝無幸位，莫不圖易思艱，庶可挽天災民變之窮，而上副引咎納言之至意。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty appoints the worthy without doubt and employs men according to their talents, so that the court has no positions obtained by favor and none fail to think of the difficult while in ease, may the extremity of heavenly calamities and popular upheaval perhaps be turned back, fulfilling to the utmost Your Majesty's purpose of accepting blame and receiving counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty appoints the worthy without hesitation and uses each man according to his gifts, so that the court holds no posts won by favor and every official thinks of hardship while living in ease, can heaven's disasters and popular unrest perhaps be reversed—and Your Majesty's purpose of accepting blame and heeding counsel be fully answered."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 三年，授兵部侍郎，署倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Board of War and served concurrently as acting Vice Commissioner of the Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Vice Minister of War and served concurrently as acting Vice Commissioner of the Granaries.

sentences.zh: 廉得奸人把持倉務，置於法。

translations.literal: Through investigation he found rascals monopolizing granary affairs and had them punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Through investigation he found rascals controlling granary affairs and had them punished by law.

sentences.zh: 十年，調工部，復調吏部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was transferred to the Board of Works, then transferred again to the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to the Board of Works, then to the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he was promoted to Minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the second year, he died; his posthumous title was Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died; his posthumous title was Wenke.

sentences.zh: =張祥河=張祥河，字詩舲，江蘇婁縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianghe, styled Shi'ting, was a native of Lou County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianghe, courtesy name Shi'ting, was from Lou County, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年進士，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing, was appointed a Grand Secretariat secretary, and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部主事，累轉郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a secretary of the Board of Revenue and rose through successive posts to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Board of Revenue as a secretary and rose in succession to director.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年，出為山東督糧道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang, he was posted out as Grain Transport Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he was posted out as Grain Transport Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢河南按察使，以父憂去官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Henan but left office on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Henan but left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服除，仍授河南按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was again appointed Judicial Commissioner of Henan and served concurrently as acting Financial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was again appointed Judicial Commissioner of Henan and served concurrently as acting Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，祥符決口合龍，賜花翎，詔以河南迭被水災，始終克勤其事，予優敘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the breach at Xiangfu was closed, he was granted the peacock feather; an edict noted that Henan had suffered repeated floods and that he had diligently persevered in the work throughout, and granted him preferential promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, after the breach at Xiangfu was closed, he received the peacock feather; an edict noted that Henan had suffered repeated floods and that he had worked diligently throughout, and granted him preferential promotion.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷廣西布政使，擢陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Guangxi and promoted to Governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Guangxi and promoted to Governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 西安、同州有刀匪擾害閭閻，祥河飭嚴捕百餘人置諸法，詔嘉之。

translations.literal: In Xi'an and Tongzhou, knife-wielding bandits harassed the populace; Xianghe ordered strict arrests, and more than a hundred were punished by law; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xi'an and Tongzhou, knife-wielding bandits terrorized the people; Xianghe ordered strict arrests, and more than a hundred were punished by law; an edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，應詔陳言，請述祖德，守成法，勵官方，蠲民欠。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, responding to the imperial call he memorialized, asking that ancestral virtue be recounted, established law be upheld, official discipline be encouraged, and popular arrears be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he answered the imperial call with a memorial asking that ancestral virtue be recounted, established law upheld, official discipline strengthened, and popular arrears remitted.

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 祥河優於文事，治尚安靜，不擾民，言者劾其性耽詩酒。

translations.literal: Xianghe was skilled in literary affairs; his administration favored quiet and did not disturb the people, but memorialists impeached him for being addicted to poetry and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghe excelled at literary affairs; his administration favored quiet and did not disturb the people, but critics impeached him for indulging in poetry and wine.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，東南軍事日棘，祥河奏言：「陝西興安等地毗連楚境，應舉行團練，擇要防堵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, as military affairs in the southeast grew daily more urgent, Xianghe memorialized: "Xing'an and other areas in Shaanxi border Chu territory; local militia training should be carried out and key points chosen for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, as military affairs in the southeast grew daily more pressing, Xianghe memorialized: "Xing'an and other districts in Shaanxi border Chu territory; militia training should be organized and key points chosen for defense.

sentences.zh: 惟鄉勇良莠不齊，易聚難散，不如力行保甲，為緝姦良法。」

translations.literal: But village braves are a mixed lot, easy to gather and hard to disperse—it would be better to vigorously enforce the baojia system, a sound method for suppressing crime."
translations.idiomatic: But village braves are a mixed lot, easy to gather and hard to disperse; it would be better to enforce the baojia system vigorously, a sound method for suppressing crime."

sentences.zh: 三年，召還京。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，授內閣學士，尋遷吏部侍郎，督順天學政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat; soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and appointed Educational Commissioner of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed a Grand Secretariat grand secretary; soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of Civil Office and appointed Educational Commissioner of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病罷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was dismissed on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 病痊，仍授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When his illness was cured, he was again appointed Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness was cured, he was again appointed Vice Minister of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢左都御史，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left and transferred to Minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and transferred to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was given the additional title of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was given the additional title of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he requested dismissal on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he requested dismissal on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，卒，諡溫和。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he died; his posthumous title was Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he died; his posthumous title was Wenhe.

sentences.zh: =羅惇衍=羅惇衍，字椒生，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Luo Dunyan, styled Jiaosheng, was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Dunyan, courtesy name Jiaosheng, was from Shunde, Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin probationer, and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十七年，督四川學政，召對，上以惇衍年少，語多土音，留不遣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Sichuan; summoned for audience, the emperor, finding Dunyan young and his speech heavily accented, kept him in the capital and did not send him out.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Sichuan; summoned for audience, the emperor, finding Dunyan young and his speech heavily accented, kept him in the capital and did not send him out.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，大考一等，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, in the triennial evaluation he received the first grade and was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he earned the first grade in the triennial evaluation and was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士，轉通政副使、太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Doctor Reader-in-Waiting, then became Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission and Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Doctor Reader-in-Waiting, then became Vice Commissioner of Transmission and Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，督安徽學政，遷通政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Anhui and promoted to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Anhui and promoted to Transmission Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文宗即位，應詔陳言，略言：「古帝王治天下，根源祗在一心，要在覽載籍，勤省察，居敬窮理，以檢攝此心。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, responding to the imperial call he memorialized, stating in part: "Ancient emperors and kings governed the realm; the root lay in a single heart—what mattered was reading the historical records, diligent self-examination, holding reverence and investigating principle to govern this heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he answered the imperial call with a memorial stating in part: "Ancient emperors and kings governed the realm; the root lay in the heart alone—what mattered was reading the records, examining oneself diligently, holding reverence and investigating principle to govern the heart.

sentences.zh: 聖祖仁皇帝御纂性理精義，於存養省察、致知力行，以及人倫性命，皆有程途階級，其論君道，尤極詳備。

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor's personally compiled Essentials of Principle and Nature sets out graduated stages for preserving and nourishing, self-examination, extending knowledge and putting it into action, and for human relations and life's nature; his discussion of the way of rulership is especially thorough and complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor's personally compiled Essentials of Principle and Nature lays out graduated stages for preserving and nourishing the self, self-examination, extending knowledge and acting on it, and for human relations and life's nature; his discussion of the way of rulership is especially thorough.

sentences.zh: 惟在皇上講習討論，身體力行。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty studies and discusses them and puts them into practice in person.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty studies and discusses them and puts them into practice in person.

sentences.zh: 世宗憲皇帝硃批諭旨，於臣工奏摺，指示得失，明見萬里。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor's vermilion rescripts on memorials from ministers indicated right and wrong with insight visible across ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor's vermilion rescripts on ministers' memorials pointed out right and wrong with insight that reached across the realm.

sentences.zh: 皇上幾暇，日閱一二事，凡督撫陳奏，如能深謀遠慮，措置得宜，即予以褎答；

translations.literal: In Your Majesty's leisure hours, read one or two cases each day: whenever governors-general and governors memorialize, if their plans are far-sighted and their arrangements apt, grant them commendation;
translations.idiomatic: In Your Majesty's leisure hours, read one or two cases each day: whenever governors-general and governors memorialize, if their plans are far-sighted and their arrangements sound, grant them commendation;

sentences.zh: 若有飾詐懷私，亦為之指示，庶大吏皆知警戒。

translations.literal: if they dissemble or harbor private aims, point this out as well, so that grand officials may all know to be on guard.
translations.idiomatic: if they dissemble or harbor private aims, point this out as well, so that grand officials may all know to be on guard.

sentences.zh: 他若御纂資政要覽、庭訓格言諸書，皆本心出治，一以貫之。

translations.literal: As for other works such as the Imperially Compiled Essential Mirror for Governance and Precepts of the Court Instruction—all proceed from the heart as the source of rule and run through as one.
translations.idiomatic: As for other works such as the Imperially Compiled Essential Mirror for Governance and Precepts of the Court Instruction—all proceed from the heart as the source of rule and run through as one.

sentences.zh: 伏原皇上法祖以修己，推而知人安民，皆得其道。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty may follow the ancestors in cultivating the self, and extending this, know men and settle the people—all in their proper way."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty follow the ancestors in cultivating the self and, extending this, know men and settle the people—all in their proper way."

sentences.zh: 又請諭部院大臣各舉所知，備京卿及講讀之任；

translations.literal: He also asked that ministers of the departments and boards be instructed each to recommend men they knew, to fill Beijing posts and lecturing and reading appointments;
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that ministers of the departments and boards each be instructed to recommend men they knew for Beijing posts and lecturing and reading appointments;

sentences.zh: 敕直省督撫、提鎮、學政皆得犯顏直諫，指陳利病，無所忌諱，籓臬亦許密封由督撫代為呈奏。

translations.literal: and that governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, garrison commanders, and educational commissioners of all provinces be ordered that all may speak bluntly and remonstrate directly, set forth benefits and harms without reserve; provincial treasurer-commissioners and judicial commissioners should also be permitted sealed memorials submitted through governors.
translations.idiomatic: and that governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, garrison commanders, and educational commissioners in every province be ordered to speak bluntly and remonstrate directly, setting forth benefits and harms without reserve; provincial treasurers and judicial commissioners should also be permitted sealed memorials submitted through governors.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and the emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，疏陳風俗侈靡，民生日困，請崇儉禁奢，以蓄物力。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, he memorialized that customs were extravagant, the people's livelihood daily more straitened, and asked that frugality be honored and luxury forbidden to conserve resources.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he memorialized that customs had grown extravagant, the people's livelihood daily more straitened, and asked that frugality be honored and luxury forbidden to conserve resources.

sentences.zh: 二年，署吏部侍郎，授左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he served as acting Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office and was appointed Associate Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served as acting Vice Minister of Civil Office and was appointed Associate Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢刑部侍郎，仍兼權吏部。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Board of Punishments while still concurrently acting for the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments while still concurrently acting for the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 時軍需孔亟，戶部令京師商民以賃舍金一月納公家，惇衍以為非政體，疏乞明定限制。

translations.literal: At the time military needs were urgent; the Board of Revenue ordered Beijing merchants and townspeople to turn over one month's rent to the government; Dunyan considered this improper to governance and memorialized asking that limits be clearly fixed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time military needs were urgent; the Board of Revenue ordered Beijing merchants and townspeople to turn over one month's rent to the government; Dunyan considered this improper to governance and memorialized asking that limits be clearly fixed.

sentences.zh: 又疏薦廣東在籍給事中蘇廷魁等任籌軍餉。

translations.literal: He also memorialized recommending Su Tingkui of Guangdong, a former memorialist-at-large, and others to raise military funds.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized recommending Su Tingkui of Guangdong, a former memorialist-at-large, and others to raise military funds.

sentences.zh: 江寧既陷，寇氛复溯江上犯，惇衍疏請敕曾國籓練楚勇，自湖南移駐武昌，杜賊窺伺荊襄；

translations.literal: After Nanjing fell and rebel pressures again surged up the Yangzi, Dunyan memorialized asking that Zeng Guofan be ordered to drill Chu braves, move from Hunan to garrison Wuchang, and block the rebels from eyeing Jing and Xiang;
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell and rebel pressure again surged up the Yangzi, Dunyan memorialized asking that Zeng Guofan be ordered to drill Chu braves, move from Hunan to garrison Wuchang, and block the rebels from eyeing Jing and Xiang;

sentences.zh: 蘇廷魁募粵勇援江西；

translations.literal: that Su Tingkui raise Guangdong braves to aid Jiangxi;
translations.idiomatic: that Su Tingkui raise Guangdong braves to aid Jiangxi;

sentences.zh: 袁甲三回河南防捻匪，並會同已革兩廣總督徐廣縉募新兵堵禦鳳、潁，遏賊北竄諸路；

translations.literal: that Yuan Jiasan return to Henan to guard against Nian bandits, and together with the dismissed Governor-General of Liangguang Xu Guangjin raise new troops to block the Feng and Ying regions and check rebel thrusts northward on all routes;
translations.idiomatic: that Yuan Jiasan return to Henan to guard against Nian bandits, and together with the dismissed Governor-General of Liangguang Xu Guangjin raise new troops to block the Feng and Ying regions and check rebel thrusts northward on all routes;

sentences.zh: 多被採納。

translations.literal: Many of these were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Many of these were adopted.

sentences.zh: 命隨同惠親王巡防京師，調戶部。

translations.literal: He was ordered to accompany Prince Yi in patrolling the defenses of the capital and was transferred to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to accompany Prince Yi in patrolling the defenses of the capital and was transferred to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年，以父憂歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he returned home on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 七年，英吉利兵攻陷廣州，八年正月，命惇衍及在籍太常寺卿龍元僖、給事中蘇廷魁為團練大臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, English troops captured Guangzhou; in the first month of the eighth year, Dunyan, together with Long Yuanxi, former Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Su Tingkui, supervising censor, were appointed militia-training commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year English troops captured Guangzhou; in the first month of the eighth year Dunyan, together with Long Yuanxi, former Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Su Tingkui, supervising censor, were appointed militia-training commissioners.

sentences.zh: 十年，款議定。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the peace settlement was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the peace settlement was concluded.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召來京，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was summoned to the capital and promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was summoned to the capital and promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，兩廣總督勞崇光被劾任用非人，調度乖方，命惇衍偕廣州將軍穆克德訥按治，崇光坐罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Governor-General of Liangguang Lao Chongguang was impeached for appointing unsuitable men and directing operations wrongly; Dunyan was ordered together with Mukedena, General of Guangzhou, to investigate, and Chongguang was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, Governor-General of Liangguang Lao Chongguang was impeached for appointing unsuitable men and directing operations wrongly; Dunyan was ordered together with Mukedena, General of Guangzhou, to investigate, and Chongguang was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書，疏言：「吏治日壞，當獎廉懲貪。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Board of Revenue and memorialized: "Official governance grows daily worse; integrity should be rewarded and corruption punished.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue and memorialized: "Official governance grows daily worse; integrity should be rewarded and corruption punished.

sentences.zh: 四川總督駱秉章、湖北巡撫嚴樹森、山西布政使鄭敦謹、山東按察使吳廷棟，清操較著，請獎之，以勵其餘。」

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor-General Luo Bingzhang, Hubei Governor Yan Shusen, Shanxi Financial Commissioner Zheng Dunjin, and Shandong Judicial Commissioner Wu Tingdong are notably upright in conduct—I ask that they be commended to encourage the rest."
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Governor-General Luo Bingzhang, Hubei Governor Yan Shusen, Shanxi Financial Commissioner Zheng Dunjin, and Shandong Judicial Commissioner Wu Tingdong are notably upright in conduct—I ask that they be commended to encourage the rest."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「皇上求賢若渴，應詔者寥寥，即有登諸薦牘者，或由他省督撫保舉，必待本省給諮，始能赴部，非所以示虛懷延攬之道。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Your Majesty seeks the worthy as if parched, yet responses to the imperial call are few; even those placed on recommendation rolls, if recommended by governors of other provinces, must wait for endorsement from their home province before proceeding to the ministry—this is not the way to show open-minded recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Your Majesty seeks the worthy as if parched, yet responses to the imperial call are few; even those placed on recommendation rolls, if recommended by governors of other provinces, must wait for endorsement from their home province before proceeding to the ministry—this is not the way to show open-minded recruitment.

sentences.zh: 且但令封​​疆大吏保舉，而未及京卿，恐馴致外重內輕，不可不防其漸。

translations.literal: Moreover, if only frontier grand officials are told to recommend men but Beijing ministers are not included, I fear this will by degrees lead to the outer growing heavy and the inner light—the trend must be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if only frontier grand officials are told to recommend men but Beijing ministers are not included, I fear this will by degrees make the outer heavy and the inner light—the trend must be guarded against.

sentences.zh: 內閣、六部、九卿等朝廷重臣，素所親信，必俾其各舉所知，眾正盈廷，然後可反危為安，轉亂為治。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat, Six Boards, Nine Chief Ministries, and other weighty ministers of the court, long trusted by Your Majesty—each must be made to recommend men they know; with the upright filling the court, only then may danger be turned to safety and chaos to order.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat, Six Boards, Nine Chief Ministries, and other weighty ministers of the court, long trusted by Your Majesty—each must be made to recommend men they know; with the upright filling the court, only then may danger be turned to safety and chaos to order.

sentences.zh: 請不必限以時日，拘以人數，但有操守廉潔，才猷卓越者，即許隨時疏薦。

translations.literal: I ask that no limit be set on time or number: whenever there is integrity and outstanding ability, memorial recommendation be permitted at any time.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that no limit be set on time or number: whenever there is integrity and outstanding ability, memorial recommendation be permitted at any time.

sentences.zh: 倘所舉之人，將來或犯貪污，罪其舉主。」

translations.literal: If men recommended later commit corruption, punish those who recommended them."
translations.idiomatic: If men recommended later commit corruption, punish those who recommended them."

sentences.zh: 二年，兼署左都御史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he served concurrently as acting Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served concurrently as acting Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼管三庫，署翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he concurrently managed the Three Treasuries and served as acting Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he concurrently managed the Three Treasuries and served as acting Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 伊犁參贊大臣聯捷、御史陳廷經先後論劾「陝西布政使林壽圖沉湎於酒，巡撫劉蓉未諳公事，舉劾悉聽壽圖」，及「蓉疏奏失體，漏洩密保」。

translations.literal: Lianjie, Imperial Resident at Ili, and Supervising Censor Chen Tingjing successively impeached: "Shaanxi Financial Commissioner Lin Shoutu is sunk in wine; Governor Liu Rong is unversed in official business and follows Shoutu in all promotions and dismissals," and "Rong's memorials are improper in form and leak confidential recommendations."
translations.idiomatic: Lianjie, Imperial Resident at Ili, and Supervising Censor Chen Tingjing successively impeached: "Shaanxi Financial Commissioner Lin Shoutu is sunk in wine; Governor Liu Rong is unversed in official business and follows Shoutu in all promotions and dismissals," and "Rong's memorials are improper in form and leak confidential recommendations."

sentences.zh: 命偕協辦大學士瑞常赴陝西按治。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Associate Grand Secretary Ruichang to go to Shaanxi to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered together with Associate Grand Secretary Ruichang to go to Shaanxi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 惇衍等為疏辨，僅以微過議處，吏議壽圖遷調，蓉革職留任。

translations.literal: Dunyan and the others submitted a memorial in their defense; only minor faults were punished; the personnel office recommended transferring Shoutu and dismissing Rong from office while retaining him in post.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyan and the others submitted a memorial in their defense; only minor faults were punished; the personnel office recommended transferring Shoutu and stripping Rong of office while retaining him in post.

sentences.zh: 尋蓉復以他事​​罷，陝民為蓉、壽圖訟冤，總督楊岳斌以聞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Rong was again dismissed for other matters; the people of Shaanxi petitioned on behalf of Rong and Shoutu, and Governor Yang Yuebin reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Rong was again dismissed for other matters; the people of Shaanxi petitioned on behalf of Rong and Shoutu, and Governor Yang Yuebin reported this.

sentences.zh: 惇衍等已回京復命覆奏，遂合疏言：「劉蓉秉性樸直，辦理甘肅潰勇，不動聲色，悉臻妥善。

translations.literal: Dunyan and the others had already returned to the capital to report; in a joint follow-up memorial they stated: "Liu Rong's nature is plain and straight; in handling the routed braves from Gansu he moved without show and brought everything to proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyan and the others had already returned to the capital to report; in a joint follow-up memorial they stated: "Liu Rong's nature is plain and straight; in handling the routed braves from Gansu he moved without show and brought everything to proper order.

sentences.zh: 甘肅亂回竄擾，遣兵分佈要隘，陝民以安。

translations.literal: When disorderly Muslims from Gansu raided and harassed, he dispatched troops to key passes and the people of Shaanxi were settled.
translations.idiomatic: When disorderly Muslims from Gansu raided and harassed, he dispatched troops to key passes and the people of Shaanxi were settled.

sentences.zh: 林壽圖身任勞怨，勤奮有為，惟參劾屬員，間有輕重失當，致謗毀紛興，而其廉潔之操，究不能稍加訾議。」

translations.literal: Lin Shoutu personally bore hardship and blame, was diligent and effective; only in impeaching subordinates he sometimes misjudged severity, which provoked slander—but his integrity cannot in the end be faulted in the least."
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shoutu personally bore hardship and blame and was diligent and effective; only in impeaching subordinates he sometimes misjudged severity, which provoked slander—but his integrity cannot in the end be faulted in the least."

sentences.zh: 詔蓉仍署巡撫，壽圖來京候簡用。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Rong continue as acting governor and that Shoutu come to the capital to await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that Rong continue as acting governor and that Shoutu come to the capital to await appointment.

sentences.zh: 六年，兼署工部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he served concurrently as acting Minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served concurrently as acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he returned home on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he died; his posthumous title was Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died; his posthumous title was Wenke.

sentences.zh: 惇衍學宗宋儒，立朝正色，抗論時事，章凡數十上，無所顧避。

translations.literal: Dunyan's learning followed the Song Neo-Confucians; in court he maintained a stern mien, disputing current affairs; he submitted dozens of memorials without stint or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyan's learning followed the Song Neo-Confucians; in court he maintained a stern mien and disputed current affairs; he submitted dozens of memorials without stint or fear.

sentences.zh: 著有集義編、百法百戒、庸言、孔子集語等書。

translations.literal: He authored works including Collected Meaning, A Hundred Laws and A Hundred Admonitions, Common Words, and Collected Sayings of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: He authored works including Collected Meaning, A Hundred Laws and A Hundred Admonitions, Common Words, and Collected Sayings of Confucius.

sentences.zh: =鄭敦謹=鄭敦謹，字小山，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Zheng Dunjin, styled Xiaoshan, was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dunjin, courtesy name Xiaoshan, was from Changsha, Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，散館授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin probationer, and upon graduation from the Hanlin was appointed Secretary of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and upon graduation was appointed a secretary of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中，出為山東登州知府，擢河南南汝光道。

translations.literal: After a second promotion to Director, he was posted out as Prefect of Dengzhou in Shandong and promoted to Circuit Intendant of Nannu and Guang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After a second promotion to director, he was posted out as Prefect of Dengzhou in Shandong and promoted to Circuit Intendant of Nannu and Guang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，泌陽土匪喬建德踞角子山，敦謹與南陽鎮總兵圖塔布督兵捕獲之，被議敘，署布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, the bandit Qiao Jiande of Biyang occupied Jiaozi Mountain; Dunjin together with Tutabu, Brigadier-General of Nanyang, directed troops and captured him; he received a citation for merit and served as acting Financial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng the bandit Qiao Jiande of Biyang occupied Jiaozi Mountain; Dunjin together with Tutabu, Brigadier-General of Nanyang, directed troops and captured him; he received a merit citation and served as acting Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，授廣東布政使，仍留署任。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Guangdong but remained to serve in his acting post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Guangdong but remained to serve in his acting post.

sentences.zh: 粵匪入湖北，命赴信陽，會南陽鎮總兵柏山扼要設防。

translations.literal: When Guangdong rebels entered Hubei, he was ordered to Xinyang and coordinated with Baishan, Brigadier-General of Nanyang, to hold key points in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong rebels entered Hubei, he was ordered to Xinyang and coordinated with Baishan, Brigadier-General of Nanyang, to hold key points in defense.

sentences.zh: 三年，命河南巡撫陸應穀統兵駐南陽，會城及信陽有事，許敦謹專摺馳奏。

translations.literal: In the third year, Henan Governor Lu Yinggu was ordered to command troops garrisoned at Nanyang; when the provincial capital or Xinyang were affected, Dunjin was permitted to submit urgent memorials directly.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Henan Governor Lu Yinggu was ordered to command troops garrisoned at Nanyang; when the provincial capital or Xinyang were affected, Dunjin was permitted to submit urgent memorials directly.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣琦善督師援安徽，檄敦謹總理信陽糧台。

translations.literal: Imperial Commissioner Qishan directed troops to aid Anhui and ordered Dunjin to oversee the grain depot at Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Qishan directed troops to aid Anhui and ordered Dunjin to oversee the grain depot at Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 及師屯江北，糧台移設徐州，仍令敦謹往任其事。

translations.literal: When the army encamped north of the Yangzi, the grain depot was moved to Xuzhou and Dunjin was still ordered to take charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the army encamped north of the Yangzi, the grain depot was moved to Xuzhou and Dunjin was still ordered to take charge.

sentences.zh: 尋調授河南布政使，留筦糧台如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred and appointed Financial Commissioner of Henan while remaining in charge of the grain depot as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred and appointed Financial Commissioner of Henan while remaining in charge of the grain depot as before.

sentences.zh: 四年，光州、陳州捻匪起，巡撫英桂出駐汝陽，詔敦謹赴本任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Nian bandits rose in Guangzhou and Chenzhou; Governor Ying Gui moved out to garrison Ruyang, and Dunjin was ordered to proceed to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Nian bandits rose in Guangzhou and Chenzhou; Governor Ying Gui moved out to garrison Ruyang, and Dunjin was ordered to proceed to his regular post.

sentences.zh: 省城戒嚴，敦謹督率官紳倡捐經費，興團練。

translations.literal: The provincial capital was placed under martial law; Dunjin supervised officials and gentry in collecting donated funds and organizing local militia.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial capital was placed under martial law; Dunjin supervised officials and gentry in collecting donated funds and organizing local militia.

sentences.zh: 皖捻犯永城、夏邑，增調兵勇防黃河各渡口，斷寇北竄。

translations.literal: When Anhui Nian raided Yongcheng and Xiayi, he added troops to guard the Yellow River crossings and block rebel thrusts northward.
translations.idiomatic: When Anhui Nian raided Yongcheng and Xiayi, he added troops to guard the Yellow River crossings and block rebel thrusts northward.

sentences.zh: 尋命暫署巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to serve temporarily as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to serve temporarily as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐欠解甘肅兩年協餉，降調。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for failure to deliver two years' cooperative pay to Gansu, he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, for failure to deliver two years' cooperative pay to Gansu, he was demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 召還京，以四品京堂候補，授太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, he awaited appointment as a fourth-rank Beijing official and was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he awaited appointment as a fourth-rank Beijing official and was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 八年，督山東學政，累遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Shandong and rose through successive posts to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Educational Commissioner of Shandong and rose in succession to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，署戶部侍郎，復出為山西布政使，調署陝西布政使，調授直隸布政使，擢河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he served as Acting Vice Minister of Revenue, went out again as Financial Commissioner of Shanxi, was transferred to serve as Acting Financial Commissioner of Shaanxi, was transferred and appointed Financial Commissioner of Zhili, and was promoted to Director-General of the East Yellow River Conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he served as Acting Vice Minister of Revenue, then returned to the provinces as Financial Commissioner of Shanxi, was transferred to act as Financial Commissioner of Shaanxi, was appointed Financial Commissioner of Zhili, and was promoted to Director-General of the East Yellow River Conservancy.

sentences.zh: 四年，授湖北巡撫，尋召授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Governor of Hubei; soon afterward he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Governor of Hubei; soon afterward he was recalled and made Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 捻匪渡河入山西境，巡撫趙長齡、按察使陳湜疏防被劾，詔敦謹往按，長齡、湜並坐罷，即命敦謹署山西巡撫。

translations.literal: Nian rebels crossed the river and entered Shanxi. Governor Zhao Changling and Surveillance Commissioner Chen Shi were impeached for negligent defense. Dunjin was ordered to investigate; Zhao and Chen were both dismissed, and Dunjin was immediately appointed Acting Governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian rebels crossed the Yellow River into Shanxi, Governor Zhao Changling and Surveillance Commissioner Chen Shi were impeached for lax defense. The court ordered Dunjin to investigate; Zhao and Chen were both removed from office, and Dunjin was immediately appointed Acting Governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 七年，出省治防，移軍駐澤州欄車鎮，為各路策應。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he left the province to manage defenses, moved his army to garrison Lanche Fort in Zezhou, and coordinated support for the various columns.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went out to manage the defenses himself, shifted his headquarters to Lanche Fort in Zezhou, and coordinated support for the various field commands.

sentences.zh: 授工部尚書，仍留署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works but continued to serve as Acting Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Works but remained Acting Governor.

sentences.zh: 回匪入河套，近邊震動。

translations.literal: Hui rebels entered the Ordos Loop; the border regions were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebels entered the Ordos Loop, and the frontier was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 敦謹移駐寧武督防，別遣兵守榆林、保德下游各隘。

translations.literal: Dunjin moved his headquarters to Ningwu to supervise defenses and dispatched troops separately to hold the passes downstream from Yulin and Baode.
translations.idiomatic: Dunjin moved to Ningwu to direct the defenses and sent separate detachments to hold the passes downstream from Yulin and Baode.

sentences.zh: 增募砲勇，補葺河曲邊牆。

translations.literal: He recruited additional artillery troops and repaired the border wall at Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: He raised additional artillery troops and repaired the border wall at Hequ.

sentences.zh: 回匪窺包頭鎮，沿河堵禦，會綏遠城將軍定安遣隊迎剿，總兵張曜自河曲截擊，破走之。

translations.literal: Hui rebels probed Baotou; defenses were set up along the river. Meanwhile General Ding'an of Suiyuancheng dispatched a column to meet and suppress them, and Brigade General Zhang Yao intercepted them from Hequ and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui rebels probed Baotou, defenses were thrown up along the river. General Ding'an of Suiyuancheng sent a column to meet them, and Brigade General Zhang Yao cut them off at Hequ and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 八年，調兵部尚書，回京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of War and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of War and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九年，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred again to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督馬新貽被刺，獲兇犯張汶祥，江寧將軍魁玉、漕運總督張之萬會讞，言汶祥為洪秀全餘黨，其戕新貽，別無主謀者。

translations.literal: Governor-General Ma Xinyi of Liangjiang was assassinated. The killer Zhang Wenxiang was captured. General Kuiyu of Jiangning and Grain Transport Director-General Zhang Zhiwan jointly reheard the case and reported that Wenxiang was a remnant of Hong Xiuquan's faction, that he had killed Xinyi, and that there was no other mastermind.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Ma Xinyi of Liangjiang was assassinated. The assassin Zhang Wenxiang was captured. General Kuiyu of Jiangning and Grain Transport Director-General Zhang Zhiwan jointly reheard the case and reported that Wenxiang was a remnant of Hong Xiuquan's forces, that he had killed Xinyi on his own, and that no other mastermind was involved.

sentences.zh: 命敦謹往會鞫，仍以初讞上，論極刑。

translations.literal: Dunjin was ordered to join in the trial; he still upheld the original verdict and recommended the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Dunjin was ordered to join the investigation; he upheld the original verdict and recommended execution.

sentences.zh: 十年春，敦謹還京，至清江浦，上疏以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Dunjin returned to the capital. When he reached Qingjiangpu he memorialized, pleading illness to resign.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year Dunjin was returning to the capital. At Qingjiangpu he memorialized, pleading illness and asking to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 光緒十一年，卒，諡恪慎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Guangxu he died and was posthumously honored with the title Késhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Guangxu reign he died and was posthumously honored with the title Késhen, "Respectful and Cautious."

sentences.zh: =龐鍾璐=龐鍾璐，字寶生，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Pang Zhonglu, styled Baosheng, was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Zhonglu, courtesy name Baosheng, was from Changshu, Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he placed third among the first-rank jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of the Daoguang reign he finished third among the top-tier jinshi and was appointed a Compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，大考一等，擢庶子，遷侍講學士，署祭酒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he earned first grade in the triennial evaluation, was promoted to Junior Tutor, transferred to Lecturer-in-Waiting, and served as Acting Chief of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign he earned the first grade in the triennial evaluation, was promoted to Junior Tutor, transferred to Lecturer-in-Waiting, and served as Acting Chief of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 明年，授光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢內閣學士，署工部侍郎，以父憂歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet, served as Acting Vice Minister of Works, and returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet, served as Acting Vice Minister of Works, and returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十年，江南大營潰，蘇、常淪陷，督團勇防禦。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Jiangnan Grand Camp collapsed and Suzhou and Changzhou fell. He directed the local militia in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Jiangnan Grand Camp collapsed and Suzhou and Changzhou fell. He took charge of the local militia in defense.

sentences.zh: 上命鍾璐陳奏軍事，鍾璐疏言：「常、昭三面皆賊，惟恃民團抵禦。

translations.literal: The throne ordered Zhonglu to report on military affairs. Zhonglu memorialized: "Changzhou and Zhaoshu are beset on three sides by rebels and rely solely on local militia for defense.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Zhonglu to report on military affairs. Zhonglu memorialized: "Changzhou and Zhaoshu are surrounded on three sides by rebels and can rely only on local militia for defense.

sentences.zh: 器械不精，紀律不明，若大兵不速至，恐裹脅愈多，愈難措手。

translations.literal: Their weapons are crude and their discipline unclear. If regular troops do not arrive soon, I fear more people will be coerced into joining the rebels, making the situation ever harder to handle.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons are poor and their discipline lax. If regular troops do not arrive soon, I fear ever more people will be swept up by coercion, and the situation will become harder to manage.

sentences.zh: 請飭督臣曾國籓迅由祁門統師南下，常、昭庫款無存，惟賴捐輸充餉，軍需浩穰，捐戶搜括無遺。

translations.literal: I beg that Governor Zeng Guofan be ordered to lead his army swiftly south from Qimen. Changzhou and Zhaoshu have no treasury reserves and depend entirely on donations for pay; military needs are immense and donors have been squeezed dry.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Governor Zeng Guofan be ordered to lead his army swiftly south from Qimen. Changzhou and Zhaoshu have no funds left in their treasuries and depend entirely on voluntary contributions for pay; military needs are enormous, and donors have already been squeezed dry.

sentences.zh: 並請飭督臣於就近完善之區，籌貲接濟。」

translations.literal: I also ask that the governor be instructed to raise funds in nearby intact districts to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: I also ask that the governor be instructed to raise funds in nearby districts that remain intact and send relief.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「江北惟通州最完善，與常、昭有脣齒之依。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In northern Jiangsu, Tongzhou alone remains intact; it stands in mutual dependence with Changzhou and Zhaoshu like lip and teeth.
